title.raw: 卷65 邢巒 李平 Volume 65: Xing Luan, Li Ping

sentences.zh: 邢巒 李平

translations.literal: Xing Luan, Li Ping
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan and Li Ping

sentences.zh: 邢巒，字洪賓，河間鄚人也。

translations.literal: Xing Luan, courtesy name Hongbin, was a native of Mo in Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan, styled Hongbin, came from Mo in Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: [1]五世祖嘏，石勒頻徵，不至。

translations.literal: [1] His fifth-generation ancestor Jia was repeatedly summoned by Shi Le but never went.
translations.idiomatic: [1] His fifth-generation forebear Jia was repeatedly summoned by Shi Le, yet refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 嘏無子，巒高祖蓋，自旁宗入後。

translations.literal: Jia had no son, and Luan's great-grandfather Gai entered the line as an heir from a collateral branch.
translations.idiomatic: As Jia had no son, Luan's great-grandfather Gai was adopted from a collateral branch to continue the line.

sentences.zh: 蓋孫穎，字宗敬，以才學知名。

translations.literal: Gai's grandson Ying, courtesy name Zongjing, was renowned for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's grandson Ying, styled Zongjing, won renown for literary and scholarly ability.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，與范陽盧玄、勃海高允等同時被徵。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, he was summoned at the same time as Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Shizu, he was summoned to court together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and others.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書侍郎，假通直常侍、寧朔將軍、平城子，銜命使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: He was later appointed Secretariat Gentleman, and given the provisional titles of Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the North, and Baron of Pingcheng, and was dispatched on a mission to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, provisionally invested as Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the North, and Baron of Pingcheng, and sent on a diplomatic mission to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 後以病還鄉里。

translations.literal: Later, because of illness, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，世祖訪穎於羣臣曰：「往憶邢穎長者，有學義，宜侍講東宮，今其人安在？」

translations.literal: After some time, Emperor Shizu inquired of his ministers about Ying, saying, "I recall in the past that Xing Ying was an elder of worth, learned and principled, fit to serve as tutor in the Eastern Palace — where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Emperor Shizu asked his ministers, "I remember Xing Ying as a worthy elder, learned and upright, well suited to instruct the crown prince — where is he now?"

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩對曰：「穎臥疾在家。」

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao replied, "Ying lies ill at home."
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao answered, "Ying is bedridden at home."

sentences.zh: 世祖遣太醫馳驛就療。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent the imperial physician post-haste to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the imperial physician by relay post to treat him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、定州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Kang.

sentences.zh: 子脩年，即巒父也，州主簿。

translations.literal: His son Xiunian, who was Luan's father, served as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiunian — Luan's father — served as provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 巒少而好學，負帙尋師，家貧厲節，遂博覽書傳。

translations.literal: Luan loved learning from youth, carrying books to seek teachers; though his family was poor he maintained strict integrity, and so came to read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Luan loved learning, shouldering bundles of books to seek out teachers; though poor, he held himself to strict standards and eventually mastered the classics and historical writings.

sentences.zh: 有文才幹略，美鬚髯，姿貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He possessed literary talent and strategic ability, with a fine beard and a very imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary gifts and strategic insight, a handsome beard, and a strikingly imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 州郡表貢，拜中書博士，遷員外散騎侍郎，為高祖所知賞。

translations.literal: The province and commandery recommended him for tribute; he was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, promoted to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and came to be known and appreciated by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by his province and commandery, he was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, then promoted to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and won the notice and favor of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 兼員外散騎常侍，使於蕭賾，還，拜通直郎，轉中書侍郎，甚見顧遇，常參座席。

translations.literal: Concurrently Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was sent on a mission to Xiao Ze; on his return he was appointed Direct Attendant, then transferred to Secretariat Gentleman, and was greatly favored, regularly taking part in imperial audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Serving concurrently as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was sent on a mission to Xiao Ze; upon returning he was made Direct Attendant, then Secretariat Gentleman, and enjoyed exceptional favor, often sharing the emperor's seat at court.

sentences.zh: 高祖因行藥至司空府南，見巒宅，遣使謂巒曰：「朝行藥至此，見卿宅乃住，東望德館，情有依然。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, while taking a medicinal stroll, came south of the Ministry of Works' office and saw Luan's residence; he sent a messenger to say to Luan, "On my morning walk for medicine I came here, saw your house, and stopped; looking east toward the Hall of Virtue, my feelings are much as before."
translations.idiomatic: While taking his medicinal walk, Emperor Gaozu came south of the Ministry of Works and saw Luan's home; he sent a messenger saying, "On my morning medicinal stroll I reached your house and paused; gazing east toward the Hall of Virtue, I feel much as I once did."

sentences.zh: 巒對曰：「陛下移構中京，方建無窮之業，臣意在與魏昇降，寧容不務永年之宅。」

translations.literal: Luan replied, "Your Majesty is relocating the capital to the Middle Capital and building an enterprise without end; this subject's wish is to rise and fall with Wei — how could I not attend to a dwelling for long years?"
translations.idiomatic: Luan answered, "Your Majesty is moving the capital to the Middle Capital and founding an enterprise without end; my wish is to rise and fall with Wei — how could I concern myself with a house meant to last forever?"

sentences.zh: 高祖謂司空穆亮、僕射李沖曰：「巒之此言，其意不小。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Minister of Works Mu Liang and Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Chong, "In this remark of Luan's, his ambition is no small thing."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told Minister of Works Mu Liang and Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Chong, "In these words of Luan's, his intent is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 有司奏策秀、孝，詔曰：「秀、孝殊問，經權異策，邢巒才清，可令策秀。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized regarding the examination of the Cultivated Talent and Filial and Incorrupt categories; the edict said, "The Cultivated Talent and Filial and Incorrupt categories have different questions, and the classics and administrative policy have different examination topics; Xing Luan's talent is clear — let him be examined for Cultivated Talent."
translations.idiomatic: When the relevant offices memorialized on examining candidates for Cultivated Talent and Filial and Incorrupt honors, the edict read, "Cultivated Talent and Filial and Incorrupt candidates face different questions, and the classics and statecraft are tested by different topics; Xing Luan's talent is lucid — let him sit for the Cultivated Talent examination."

sentences.zh: 後兼黃門郎。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 從征漢北，巒在新野，後至。

translations.literal: On the campaign north of the Han River, Luan was at Xinye and arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign north of the Han River, Luan was at Xinye and arrived late.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「伯玉天迷其心，鬼惑其慮，守危邦，固逆主，乃至如此。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Boyu — heaven has deluded his heart, ghosts have bewildered his plans; he holds a doomed state and clings to a rebellious lord, and has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "Boyu — heaven has clouded his mind and ghosts his judgment; he defends a doomed state for a rebellious master, and matters have reached this pass."

sentences.zh: 巒曰：「新野既摧，眾城悉潰，唯有伯玉，不識危機，平殄之辰，事在旦夕。」

translations.literal: Luan said, "Xinye already destroyed, the other cities all collapsed — only Boyu fails to see the crisis; the day of total annihilation is a matter of morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: Luan replied, "With Xinye already fallen and the other cities all routed, only Boyu does not recognize the crisis; the hour of complete destruction is near at hand."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「至此以來，雖未擒滅，城隍已崩，想在不遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "From the time we arrived here, though we have not yet captured and destroyed them, the walls and moats have already crumbled — I think it cannot be far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "Since we arrived, though we have not yet captured them outright, their walls and moats have already collapsed — I expect the end is not far off.

sentences.zh: 所以緩攻者，正待中書為露布耳。」

translations.literal: The reason we have slowed the assault is precisely to wait for the Secretariat to compose the victory bulletin."
translations.idiomatic: The reason we have eased the assault is precisely to wait for the Secretariat to draft the victory proclamation."

sentences.zh: 尋除正黃門、兼御史中尉、瀛州大中正，遷散騎常侍、兼尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Coordinator of Yingzhou; he was promoted to Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yingzhou, then promoted to Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，巒奏曰：「臣聞昔者明王之以德治天下，莫不重粟帛，輕金寶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, Luan memorialized, saying, "Your subject has heard that in antiquity enlightened kings governed the realm through virtue, and none failed to value grain and silk while holding gold and jewels lightly.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Emperor Shizong's reign, Luan submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the enlightened kings of old governed the realm through virtue, and all of them prized grain and silk while treating gold and treasure lightly.

sentences.zh: 然粟帛安國育民之方，金玉是虛華損德之物。

translations.literal: Yet grain and silk are the means to secure the state and nurture the people; gold and jade are empty show that erodes virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and silk are the means to secure the state and nurture the people; gold and jade are vain display that undermines virtue.

sentences.zh: 故先皇深觀古今，去諸奢侈。

translations.literal: Therefore the late emperor deeply observed past and present and cast off extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the late emperor looked deeply into past and present and cast off every extravagance.

sentences.zh: 服御尚質，不貴雕鏤，所珍在素，不務奇綺，至乃以紙絹為帳扆，銅鐵為轡勒。

translations.literal: For dress and use he favored simplicity, not valuing carving and inlay; what he treasured was plainness, not pursuing strange brocades — to the point of using paper and silk for screens and curtains, and copper and iron for bridle and bit.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred plainness in dress and furnishings, not prizing carving and inlay; what he valued was simplicity, not exotic silks — even using paper and silk for screens and curtains, and copper and iron for bridle and bit.

sentences.zh: 訓朝廷以節儉，示百姓以憂務，日夜孜孜，小大必慎。

translations.literal: He trained the court in frugality and showed the common people the weight of public duty, diligent day and night, careful in matters great and small.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the court in frugality and showed the people the seriousness of public affairs, toiling day and night and taking care in matters great and small.

sentences.zh: 輕賤珠璣，示其無設，府藏之金，裁給而已，更不買積以費國資。

translations.literal: He held pearls and gems cheap, showing that he had no use for them; the gold in the treasury was allotted only as needed, and no longer bought up and hoarded to drain the state's resources.
translations.idiomatic: He despised pearls and gems, showing he had no need of them; gold in the treasury was allotted only as required, and was no longer bought up and hoarded to waste the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 逮景明之初，承升平之業，四疆清晏，遠邇來同，於是蕃貢繼路，商賈交入，諸所獻貿，倍多於常。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Jingming era, inheriting an age of peace, the four frontiers were tranquil and distant and near alike came in submission; then tribute from the borderlands followed one envoy after another, merchants entered in succession, and all goods offered and traded were more than twice the usual amount.
translations.idiomatic: By the opening of the Jingming era, inheriting an age of peace, the four frontiers were calm and near and far alike submitted; tribute from the borderlands followed in unbroken succession, merchants poured in, and goods offered and traded were more than double the usual.

sentences.zh: 雖加以節約，猶歲損萬計，珍貨常有餘，國用恒不足。

translations.literal: Even with added restraint, the annual loss still ran to tens of thousands; precious goods were constantly in surplus while state expenditure was perpetually insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even with added economy, losses still ran to tens of thousands each year; precious goods were always in surplus while state funds were perpetually short.

sentences.zh: 若不裁其分限，便恐無以支歲。

translations.literal: If we do not cut their allotted shares, I fear we will be unable to meet the year's needs.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not cut back their allotted shares, I fear we will be unable to sustain the year's expenditure.

sentences.zh: 自今非為要須者，請皆不受。」

translations.literal: From now on, what is not truly necessary — please accept none of it."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, unless truly necessary, please accept nothing at all."

sentences.zh: 世宗從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋正尚書，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made full Director of the Department of State Affairs, his rank as Regular Attendant remaining unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed full Director of the Department of State Affairs, retaining his rank as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍梁秦二州行事夏侯道遷以漢中內附，詔加巒使持節、都督征梁漢諸軍事、假鎮西將軍，進退徵攝，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Xiahou Daqian, acting governor of Liang and Qin provinces for Xiao Yan, submitted Hanzhong to Wei; an edict added to Luan's commission: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs for the Campaign against Liang and Han, and Provisional General Who Pacifies the West, with authority to advance and withdraw, summon and command, and act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Daqian, Xiao Yan's acting governor of Liang and Qin provinces, submitted Hanzhong to Wei, an edict added to Luan's commission: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs for the Campaign against Liang and Han, and Provisional General Who Pacifies the West, with power to advance and withdraw, summon and command, and act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 巒至漢中，白馬已西猶未歸順，巒遣寧遠將軍楊舉、統軍楊眾愛、汜洪雅等領卒六千討之。

translations.literal: When Luan reached Hanzhong, the region west of Baima had still not submitted; Luan sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Yang Ju, Army Commander Yang Zhong'ai, Si Hongya, and others leading six thousand soldiers to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan reached Hanzhong, the country west of Baima had not yet submitted; he sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Yang Ju, Army Commander Yang Zhong'ai, Si Hongya, and others at the head of six thousand troops to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 軍鋒所臨，賊皆款附，唯補谷戍主何法靜據城拒守。

translations.literal: Wherever the army's vanguard arrived, the rebels all submitted in good faith; only He Fajing, commander of Bugu garrison, held the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the army's vanguard reached, the enemy submitted in good faith; only He Fajing, commander of Bugu garrison, held his city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 舉等進師討之，[2]法靜奔潰，乘勝追奔至關城之下，蕭衍龍驤將軍關城流雜

translations.literal: Ju and the others advanced to attack; [2] Fajing fled in rout; pursuing the victory in flight they reached below Guancheng, where Xiao Yan's General of the Flying Dragon Guancheng Liuza
translations.idiomatic: Ju and the others marched to attack; [2] Fajing broke and fled; pressing the pursuit they came beneath Guancheng, where Xiao Yan's General of the Flying Dragon — the text here reads Guancheng liu za —

translations.literal: 〈doubtful reading〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Textual note: the reading here is doubtful.〉

sentences.zh: 李侍叔逆以城降。

translations.literal: Li Shishu came out in opposition and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shishu came out to oppose them and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍輔國將軍任僧幼等三十餘將，率南安、廣長、東洛、大寒、武始、除口、平溪、桶谷諸郡之民七千餘戶，相繼而至。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Ren Sengyou and more than thirty other generals led over seven thousand households from the commanderies of Nan'an, Guangchang, Dongluo, Dahan, Wushi, Chukou, Pingxi, and Tonggu, arriving in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Ren Sengyou and more than thirty other generals led over seven thousand households from Nan'an, Guangchang, Dongluo, Dahan, Wushi, Chukou, Pingxi, Tonggu, and other commanderies, arriving in succession.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍平西將軍李天賜、晉壽太守王景胤等擁眾七千，屯據石亭。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the West Li Tianci, Administrator of Jinshou Wang Jingyin, and others mustered seven thousand men and encamped at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the West Li Tianci, Administrator of Jinshou Wang Jingyin, and others gathered seven thousand men and encamped at Shiting.

sentences.zh: 統軍韓多寶等率眾擊之，破天賜前軍趙䐗，擒斬一千三百。

translations.literal: Army Commander Han Duobao and others led troops to attack them, defeated Tianci's vanguard Zhao Qi, and captured and killed thirteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Army Commander Han Duobao and others led troops against them, routed Tianci's vanguard Zhao Qi, and captured and killed thirteen hundred men.

sentences.zh: 遣統軍李義珍討晉壽，景胤宵遁，遂平之。

translations.literal: He sent Army Commander Li Yizhen to attack Jinshou; Jingyin fled by night, and the place was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Army Commander Li Yizhen against Jinshou; Jingyin fled by night, and the district was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「巒至彼，須有板官，以懷初附，高下品第，可依征義陽都督之格也。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "When Luan arrives there, provisional officials will be needed to win over those newly submitting; ranks high and low may follow the standards used for the commander who took Yiyang."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "When Luan arrives, provisional appointments will be needed to reassure those newly submitting; grades high and low may follow the standards used for the commander who took Yiyang."

sentences.zh: 拜巒使持節、安西將軍、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Luan was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was invested Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍巴西太守龐景民恃遠不降，巒遣巴州刺史嚴玄思往攻之，斬景民，巴西悉平。

translations.literal: Pang Jingmin, Xiao Yan's Administrator of Baxi, relied on the distance and would not submit; Luan sent Yan Xuansi, Governor of Ba province, to attack him, beheaded Jingmin, and Baxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jingmin, Xiao Yan's Administrator of Baxi, trusting in the distance, refused to submit; Luan sent Yan Xuansi, Governor of Ba province, to attack him, executed Jingmin, and Baxi was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍孔陵等率眾二萬，屯據深坑，冠軍將軍魯方達固南安，[3]冠軍將軍任僧褒、輔國將軍李畎戍石同。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Conquers the Enemy Kong Ling and others with twenty thousand men to encamp at Shenkeng; General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Fangda held Nan'an; [3] General Who Conquers the Enemy Ren Sengbao and General Who Assists the State Li Qu defended Shitong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Conquers the Enemy Kong Ling and others with twenty thousand men to hold Shenkeng; General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Fangda fortified Nan'an; [3] General Who Conquers the Enemy Ren Sengbao and General Who Assists the State Li Qu garrisoned Shitong.

sentences.zh: 巒統軍王足所在擊破之，梟衍輔國將軍樂保明、寧朔將軍李伯度、龍驤將軍李思賢，賊遂保回車柵。

translations.literal: Wherever Luan's army commander Wang Zu went he defeated them, displaying the heads of Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Yue Baoming, General Who Pacifies the North Li Bodo, and General of the Flying Dragon Li Sixian; the rebels then held Huiche stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Luan's army commander Wang Zu advanced he broke the enemy, taking the heads of Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Yue Baoming, General Who Pacifies the North Li Bodo, and General of the Flying Dragon Li Sixian; the enemy then withdrew to Huiche stockade.

sentences.zh: 足又進擊衍輔國將軍范峻，自餘斬獲殆將萬數。

translations.literal: Zu again advanced against Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fan Jun; besides these, those slain and captured nearly reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zu advanced again against Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fan Jun; beyond these, those killed and captured approached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 孔陵等收集遺眾，奔保梓潼，足又破之，斬衍輔國將軍符伯度，其殺傷投溺者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Kong Ling and the others gathered the scattered remnant and fled to hold Zitong; Zu again defeated them and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fu Bodo; those killed, wounded, and drowned exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ling and the others rallied the scattered remnant and fled to Zitong; Zu defeated them again and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fu Bodo; those killed, wounded, and drowned numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 開地定民，東西七百，南北千里，獲郡十四、二部護軍及諸縣戍，遂逼涪城。

translations.literal: Opening territory and settling the people, seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south, they took fourteen commanderies, two Protectorates, and various county garrisons, and pressed on to Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: They opened territory and settled the people across seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south, captured fourteen commanderies, two Protectorates, and various county garrisons, and pressed on to Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 巒表曰：

translations.literal: Luan submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Luan submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 揚州、成都相去萬里，陸途既絕，唯資水路。

translations.literal: Yangzhou and Chengdu are ten thousand li apart; the land route is already cut off, and only the water route remains.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou and Chengdu lie ten thousand li apart; the land route is already severed, and only the water route remains.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍兄子淵藻，去年四月十三日發揚州，今歲四月四日至蜀。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's nephew Yuanzao set out from Yangzhou on the thirteenth day of the fourth month last year and reached Shu on the fourth day of the fourth month this year.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's nephew Yuanzao left Yangzhou on the thirteenth day of the fourth month last year and reached Shu on the fourth day of the fourth month this year.

sentences.zh: 水軍西上，非周年不達，外無軍援，一可圖也。

translations.literal: For the navy to go upstream takes no less than a full year; with no military aid from outside, this is the first reason the region can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: An upstream naval march takes at least a full year; with no outside military aid, this is the first reason the region can be taken.

sentences.zh: 益州頃經劉季連反叛，鄧元起攻圍，資儲散盡，倉庫空竭，今猶未復，兼民人喪膽，無復固守之意，二可圖也。

translations.literal: Yizhou has recently suffered Liu Jilian's rebellion; Deng Yuanqi besieged it until stores were scattered and granaries emptied — they have still not recovered; moreover the people have lost their courage and no longer wish to hold firm — this is the second reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou has lately endured Liu Jilian's rebellion; Deng Yuanqi besieged it until supplies were spent and the granaries empty — recovery is still incomplete; moreover the people have lost heart and no longer mean to hold firm — this is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 蕭淵藻是裙屐少年，[4]未洽治務，及至益州，便戮鄧元起、[5]曹亮宗，臨戎斬將，則是駕馭失方。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuanzao is a sandal-and-clogs youth; [4] unversed in governing affairs — once he reached Yizhou he executed Deng Yuanqi [5] and Cao Liangzong; to execute generals on the eve of battle is to mishandle the reins of command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuanzao is a pampered young fop; [4] unseasoned in governance — upon reaching Yizhou he put Deng Yuanqi [5] and Cao Liangzong to death; to behead generals on the eve of battle is to lose control of command.

sentences.zh: 范國惠津渠退敗，鎖執在獄。

translations.literal: Fan Guohui was defeated at the Jinqu canal and is bound in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Guohui was defeated at the Jinqu canal and is shackled in prison.

sentences.zh: 今之所任，並非宿將重名，皆是左右少年而已，既不厭民望，多行殘暴，民心離解，三可圖也。

translations.literal: Those now in office are none of them veteran commanders of great name — all are young men from the inner circle; they satisfy neither public expectation and often act with cruelty; the people's hearts are divided — this is the third reason.
translations.idiomatic: Those now in office are none of them seasoned commanders of renown — all are young favorites from the inner circle; they meet neither public expectation and often act with brutality; popular loyalty is breaking apart — this is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 蜀之所恃唯劍閣，今既克南安，已奪其險，據彼界內，三分已一。

translations.literal: Shu relies solely on Jian'ge Pass; now that Nan'an is taken, its strongpoint is lost; within their borders, one third is already ours.
translations.idiomatic: Shu relies solely on Jian'ge Pass; with Nan'an already taken, that strongpoint is lost; within their borders, a third is already ours.

sentences.zh: 從南安向涪，方軌任意，前軍累破，後眾喪魂，四可圖也。

translations.literal: From Nan'an toward Fu the road is open as one chooses; the vanguard has repeatedly won and the rear ranks have lost heart — this is the fourth reason.
translations.idiomatic: From Nan'an toward Fu the road lies open at will; the vanguard has won again and again while the rear ranks have lost their nerve — this is the fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 昔劉禪據一國之地，姜維為佐，鄧艾既出綿竹，彼即投降。

translations.literal: Formerly Liu Shan held a whole kingdom and Jiang Wei served as his aide; once Deng Ai emerged from Mianzhu, they at once surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Liu Shan held an entire kingdom with Jiang Wei as his chief aide; once Deng Ai marched out of Mianzhu, they surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅之世，楊安、朱彤三月取漢中，四月至涪城，兵未及州，仲孫逃命。

translations.literal: In the time of Fu Jian, Yang An and Zhu Tong took Hanzhong in the third month and reached Fucheng in the fourth; the army had not yet reached the provincial capital when Zhongsun fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: In Fu Jian's day, Yang An and Zhu Tong took Hanzhong in the third month and reached Fucheng in the fourth; before the army even reached the provincial capital, Zhongsun fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 桓溫西征，不旬月而平。

translations.literal: Huan Wen's western campaign pacified the region in less than ten months.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's western expedition pacified the region in less than ten months.

sentences.zh: 蜀地昔來恒多不守。

translations.literal: The land of Shu has always been hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: The land of Shu has always been difficult to hold.

sentences.zh: 況淵藻是蕭衍兄子，骨肉至親，若其逃亡，當無死理。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's nephew, bone and flesh most close — if he flees, there should be no reason for him to die.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's own nephew, kin of the closest degree — if he flees, he ought not to face death.

sentences.zh: 脫軍克涪城，淵藻復何宜城中坐而受困？

translations.literal: If our army takes Fucheng, how should Yuanzao sit in the city and accept encirclement?
translations.idiomatic: If our army captures Fucheng, how can Yuanzao remain in the city and accept siege?

sentences.zh: 若其出鬬，庸蜀之卒唯便刀矟，弓箭至少，假有遙射，弗至傷人，五可圖也。

translations.literal: If he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Yong and Shu are skilled only with short blades and spears; bows and arrows are few — even if they shoot from afar, they will hardly wound a man — this is the fifth reason.
translations.idiomatic: If he comes out to give battle, the troops of Yong and Shu are handy only with short blades and spears; bows and arrows are scarce — even at long range they will hardly harm a man — this is the fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 臣聞乘機而動，武之善經；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that to move according to opportunity is the finest principle of warfare;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to act when opportunity presents itself is the supreme principle of war;

sentences.zh: 攻昧侮亡，春秋明義。

translations.literal: to attack the benighted and despise the doomed is the clear teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: to strike the benighted and despise the perishing is the explicit teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 未有捨干戚而康時，不征伐而混一。

translations.literal: Never yet has an age been made secure by laying aside arms, or the realm unified without campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has an age been secured by laying aside arms, or the realm unified without campaigning.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下纂武文之業，當必世之期，跨中州之饒，兼甲兵之盛，清蕩天區，在於今矣。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty inherits the enterprise of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen, stands at the destined age of certain triumph, spans the riches of the Central Provinces and the strength of armored hosts — to sweep clean the heavenly realm is a task for today.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty inherits the enterprise of Emperors Wu and Wen, stands at the destined hour of certain triumph, commands the wealth of the Central Provinces and the might of armored hosts — to sweep clean the heavenly realm is work for this day.

sentences.zh: 是以踐極之初，壽春馳款；

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of your accession, Shouchun came in submission;
translations.idiomatic: Thus at the beginning of your accession Shouchun submitted;

sentences.zh: 先歲命將，義陽克闢。

translations.literal: last year you dispatched generals and Yiyang was taken.
translations.idiomatic: last year you dispatched generals and Yiyang was opened.

sentences.zh: 淮外謐以風清，荊沔於焉肅晏。

translations.literal: Beyond the Huai the region grew calm as wind cleared the mist; Jing and Mian were thereby stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Huai the land grew tranquil as mist cleared in the wind; Jing and Mian were thereby stilled.

sentences.zh: 方欲偃甲息兵，候機而動，而天贊休明，時來斯速，雖欲靖戎，理不獲已。

translations.literal: Just as you wished to sheathe arms and rest the troops, waiting for the moment to act, heaven favored this bright age and the time came swiftly; though you wished to still the spear, reason would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Just as you wished to sheathe arms and rest the troops, awaiting the moment to strike, heaven favored this bright age and the hour came swiftly; though you wished to still the spear, reason would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 至使道遷歸誠，漢境佇拔。

translations.literal: Hence Daqian came in loyalty and the Han frontier awaited liberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Daqian submitted in loyalty and the Han frontier awaited deliverance.

sentences.zh: 臣以不才，屬當戎寄，內省文吏，不以軍謀自許，指臨漢中，惟規保疆守界。

translations.literal: Your subject, lacking talent, has been entrusted with military command; looking within, I am a civil clerk and do not claim mastery of military strategy — facing Hanzhong, I had intended only to secure the borders and hold the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, lacking talent, has been entrusted with military command; looking within, I am a civil clerk and do not claim mastery of strategy — facing Hanzhong, I intended only to secure the borders and hold the line.

sentences.zh: 事屬艱途，東西寇竊，上憑國威，下仗將士，邊帥用命，頻有薄捷。

translations.literal: The affair lay on a hard road; bandits raided east and west; relying above on the state's might and below on the generals and soldiers, the frontier commanders obeyed orders and there were repeated small victories.
translations.idiomatic: The task lay on a hard road; enemies raided east and west; relying above on the state's might and below on officers and men, the frontier commanders obeyed orders and there were repeated minor victories.

sentences.zh: 藉勢乘威，經度大劍，既克南安，據彼要險，前軍長邁，已至梓潼，新化之民，翻然懷惠，瞻望涪益，旦夕可屠。

translations.literal: Borrowing momentum and riding prestige, we crossed the Great Sword Pass; having taken Nan'an and seized their key strongpoint, the vanguard pressed far forward and has already reached Zitong; the newly pacified people have turned in gratitude, and looking toward Fu and Yi, the cities may be taken within days.
translations.idiomatic: Borrowing momentum and riding prestige, we crossed the Great Sword Pass; with Nan'an taken and their key strongpoint seized, the vanguard has pressed far forward to Zitong; the newly pacified people have turned in gratitude, and gazing toward Fu and Yi, those cities may fall within days.

sentences.zh: 正以兵少糧匱，未宜前出。

translations.literal: It is precisely because troops are few and grain scarce that we should not advance yet.
translations.idiomatic: Precisely because troops are few and grain scarce, we ought not advance yet.

sentences.zh: 為爾稽緩，懼失民心，則更為寇。

translations.literal: For this delay I fear losing the people's hearts — then they would turn rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: For this delay I fear losing popular loyalty — then they would become rebels again.

sentences.zh: 今若不取，後圖便難，輒率愚管，庶幾殄克，如其無功，分受憲坐。

translations.literal: If we do not take it now, later plans will be hard; I venture to offer my humble counsel, hoping for total victory; if there is no success, let me share the punishment due.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take it now, later plans will be difficult; I venture my humble counsel, hoping for complete victory; if I fail, let me bear the punishment.

sentences.zh: 且益州殷實，戶餘十萬，比壽春、義陽三倍非匹，可乘可利，實在于茲。

translations.literal: Moreover Yizhou is rich and solid, with more than a hundred thousand households — three times what Shouchun and Yiyang offer, not to be compared — the opportunity and the profit truly lie here.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yizhou is rich and strong, with more than a hundred thousand households — three times the prize of Shouchun and Yiyang, incomparably greater — the opportunity and profit truly lie here.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷志存保民，未欲經略，臣之在此，便為無事，乞歸侍養，微展烏鳥。

translations.literal: If the court's aim is to preserve the people and does not yet wish to undertake conquest, then my presence here is idle; I beg to return and serve my parents, in slight fulfillment of the crow's filial duty."
translations.idiomatic: If the court's aim is to preserve the people and not yet to undertake conquest, then my presence here is idle; I beg leave to return and care for my parents, in small fulfillment of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「若賊敢闚𨵦，觀機翦撲；

translations.literal: An edict said, "If the enemy dares to peer at the frontier, watch for the moment and cut them down;
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "If the enemy dares to threaten the frontier, watch for the moment and cut them down;

sentences.zh: 如其無也，則安民保境，以悅邊心。

translations.literal: if not, then secure the people and hold the borders to satisfy the frontier's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: if not, then secure the people and hold the borders to satisfy the frontier.

sentences.zh: 子蜀之舉，更聽後敕。

translations.literal: The campaign to take Shu — await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: As for the campaign to take Shu, await further orders.

sentences.zh: 方將席卷岷蜀，電掃西南，何得辭以戀親，中途告退！

translations.literal: We are about to roll up Min and Shu and sweep the southwest like lightning — how can you plead love of kin and ask to withdraw halfway!
translations.idiomatic: We are about to roll up Min and Shu and sweep the southwest like lightning — how can you plead attachment to kin and ask to withdraw midway!

sentences.zh: 宜勗令圖，務申高略。」

translations.literal: You should be urged to plan further and fully declare your high strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Press on with your plans and fully declare your grand strategy."

sentences.zh: 巒又表曰：

translations.literal: Luan submitted another memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 昔鄧艾、鍾會率十八萬眾，傾中國資給，裁得平蜀，所以然者，鬬實力故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and exhausted the resources of the Central States, and only then pacified Shu — the reason was that they fought on equal strength.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and exhausted the resources of the Central States before they pacified Shu — because they fought against equal strength.

sentences.zh: 況臣才絕古人，智勇又闕，復何宜請二萬之眾而希平蜀？

translations.literal: How much less should I, whose talent falls short of the ancients and whose wisdom and courage are lacking, ask for twenty thousand men and hope to pacify Shu?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should I, whose talent falls far short of the ancients and whose wisdom and courage are lacking, ask for twenty thousand men and hope to pacify Shu?

sentences.zh: 所以敢者，正以據得要險，士民慕義，此往則易，彼來則難，任力而行，理有可克。

translations.literal: The reason I dare is precisely that we hold the key strongpoints and the gentry and people incline to righteousness — going there is easy, coming here is hard; acting according to strength, reason allows success.
translations.idiomatic: I dare only because we hold the key strongpoints and the gentry and people incline to us — the advance is easy for us, the return hard for them; acting according to strength, success is reasonable.

sentences.zh: 今王足前進，已逼涪城，脫得涪城，則益州便是成擒之物，但得之有早晚耳。

translations.literal: Now Wang Zu has advanced and already presses Fucheng; if Fucheng is taken, Yizhou becomes something already in hand — only a matter of sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Zu has advanced and already presses Fucheng; once Fucheng falls, Yizhou becomes prey already in hand — only a question of sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 且梓潼已附，民戶數萬，朝廷豈得不守之也？

translations.literal: Moreover Zitong has already submitted, with tens of thousands of households — can the court fail to hold it?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zitong has already submitted, with tens of thousands of households — can the court leave it unheld?

sentences.zh: 若守也，直保境之兵則已一萬，臣今請二萬伍千，所增無幾。

translations.literal: If we hold it, the troops needed merely to secure the border already come to ten thousand; I now ask for twenty-five thousand — the increase is slight.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold it, troops merely to secure the border already number ten thousand; I now ask for twenty-five thousand — the increase is small.

sentences.zh: 又劍閣天險，古來所稱，張載銘云：「世亂則逆，世清斯順。」

translations.literal: Moreover Jian'ge Pass is heaven's barrier, famed since antiquity; Zhang Zai's inscription says, "When the age is chaotic it turns against you; when the age is clear it submits."
translations.idiomatic: Jian'ge Pass is heaven's barrier, famed since antiquity; Zhang Zai's inscription reads, "In chaotic times it defies you; in ordered times it submits."

sentences.zh: 此之一言，良可惜矣。

translations.literal: In this one phrase there is much to regret."
translations.idiomatic: That single line is deeply regrettable.

sentences.zh: 臣誠知征戎危事，不易可為，自軍度劍閣以來，鬢髮中白，憂慮戰懼，寧可一日為心。

translations.literal: Your subject truly knows that campaigning is perilous and not easily done; since the army crossed Jian'ge Pass, half my hair has turned white — worry, fear, and dread for battle have never left my heart for a day.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that campaigning is perilous and not easily done; since the army crossed Jian'ge Pass, half my hair has turned white — worry, dread, and fear of battle have never left my heart for a day.

sentences.zh: 所以勉強者，既得此地而自退不守，恐辜先皇之恩遇，負陛下之爵祿，是以孜孜，頻有陳請。

translations.literal: The reason I force myself on is that having gained this territory and then withdrawing without holding it, I fear failing the late emperor's grace and betraying Your Majesty's rank and stipend — therefore I toil on and have repeatedly submitted requests.
translations.idiomatic: I force myself onward because, having gained this territory and then withdrawing without holding it, I fear failing the late emperor's grace and betraying Your Majesty's rank and stipend — therefore I press on and have repeatedly petitioned.

sentences.zh: 且臣之意算，正欲先圖涪城，以漸而進。

translations.literal: Moreover my plan is precisely to take Fucheng first and advance step by step.
translations.idiomatic: My plan is precisely to take Fucheng first and advance by stages.

sentences.zh: 若克涪城，便是中分益州之地，斷水陸之衝，彼外無援軍，孤城自守，復何能持久哉！

translations.literal: If Fucheng is taken, we will have halved the territory of Yizhou and severed the water and land routes; with no aid from outside, what lone city can hold out long?
translations.idiomatic: If Fucheng falls, we halve Yizhou and sever its water and land routes; with no outside aid, how long can a lone city hold?

sentences.zh: 臣今欲使軍軍相次，聲勢連接，先作萬全之計，然後圖彼，得之則大克，不得則自全。

translations.literal: Your subject now wishes to array the armies in succession, linking their momentum, first making plans for complete safety and then striking — if we gain it, great victory; if not, we preserve ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to array the armies in succession, linking their momentum, first securing every contingency and then striking — success brings great victory; failure still preserves us.

sentences.zh: 又巴西、南鄭相離一千四百，去州迢遞，恒多生動。

translations.literal: Moreover Baxi and Nanzheng lie fourteen hundred li apart, far from the provincial capital, and unrest constantly arises.
translations.idiomatic: Baxi and Nanzheng lie fourteen hundred li apart, far from the provincial capital, and unrest constantly flares.

sentences.zh: 昔在南之日，以其統綰勢難，故增立巴州，鎮靜夷獠，梁州藉利，因而表罷。

translations.literal: In former days in the south, because unified control was difficult, Ba province was added to quiet the Yi and Liao peoples; Liang province benefited and therefore a memorial was submitted to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the south, because unified control was difficult, Ba province was added to quiet the Yi and Liao peoples; Liang province profited and therefore a memorial was submitted to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 彼土民望，嚴、蒲、何、楊，非唯五三，族落雖在山居，而多有豪右，文學箋啟，往往可觀，冠帶風流，亦為不少。

translations.literal: The leading families of that land — Yan, Pu, He, Yang, not merely five or three — though their clans dwell in the mountains, many are powerful gentry; their literary petitions are often admirable, and men of rank and culture are not few.
translations.idiomatic: The leading families of that land — Yan, Pu, He, Yang, and more than a handful besides — though their clans dwell in the hills, many are powerful gentry; their literary petitions are often admirable, and men of rank and culture are not few.

sentences.zh: 但以去州既遠，不能仕進，至於州綱，無由厠迹。

translations.literal: But because they are far from the provincial capital they cannot advance in office; as for the provincial hierarchy, they have no way to enter it.
translations.idiomatic: But because they are far from the provincial capital they cannot advance in office; as for the provincial hierarchy, they have no path into it.

sentences.zh: 巴境民豪，便是無梁州之分，是以鬱怏，多生動靜。

translations.literal: The powerful families of Ba territory thus have no share in Liang province — hence their resentment and frequent unrest.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful families of Ba territory thus have no share in Liang province — hence their resentment and frequent disturbances.

sentences.zh: 比建議之始，[6]嚴玄思自號巴州刺史，克城以來，仍使行事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of this proposal, [6] Yan Xuansi styled himself Governor of Ba province; since the city was taken he has continued to act in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of this proposal, [6] Yan Xuansi styled himself Governor of Ba province; since the city was taken he has continued to serve in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 巴西廣袤一千，戶餘四萬，若彼立州，鎮攝華獠，則大帖民情。

translations.literal: Baxi spans a thousand li with more than forty thousand households; if a province is established there to govern the Chinese and the Liao, popular sentiment would be greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Baxi spans a thousand li with more than forty thousand households; if a province were established there to govern Chinese and tribal peoples, popular sentiment would be greatly settled.

sentences.zh: 從墊江已還，不復勞征，自為國有。

translations.literal: From Dianjiang back, no further campaigns would be needed — it would belong to the state of itself.
translations.idiomatic: From Dianjiang westward, no further campaigns would be needed — it would belong to the state of itself.

sentences.zh: 世宗不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong did not approve.

sentences.zh: 又王足於涪城輒還，遂不定蜀。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Zu withdrew from Fucheng on his own initiative, and Shu was not pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Zu withdrew from Fucheng on his own, and Shu was not pacified.

sentences.zh: 巒既克巴西，遣軍主李仲遷守之。

translations.literal: After Luan had taken Baxi, he sent Army Commander Li Zhongqian to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan took Baxi, he sent Army Commander Li Zhongqian to hold it.

sentences.zh: 仲遷得蕭衍將張法養女，有美色，甚惑之。

translations.literal: Zhongqian obtained the daughter of Xiao Yan's general Zhang Fayang — a great beauty — and was deeply infatuated with her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqian obtained the daughter of Xiao Yan's general Zhang Fayang, a woman of great beauty, and was deeply infatuated.

sentences.zh: 散費兵儲，專心酒色，公事諮承，無能見者。

translations.literal: He squandered military stores, giving himself wholly to wine and women; when official business was submitted for consultation, none could gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: He squandered military stores, devoting himself wholly to wine and women; when official business was submitted, none could reach him.

sentences.zh: 巒忿之切齒，仲遷懼，謀叛，城人斬其首，以城降衍將譙希遠，巴西遂沒。

translations.literal: Luan gnashed his teeth in rage; Zhongqian feared and plotted rebellion; the people of the city cut off his head and surrendered the city to Xiao Yan's general Qiao Xiyuan — Baxi was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Luan gnashed his teeth in fury; Zhongqian feared and plotted rebellion; the townspeople cut off his head and surrendered to Xiao Yan's general Qiao Xiyuan — Baxi was lost.

sentences.zh: 武興氐楊集起等反叛，巒遣統軍傅豎眼討平之，語在豎眼傳。

translations.literal: The Di of Wuxing, Yang Jiqing and others, rebelled; Luan sent Army Commander Fu Shuyan to suppress and pacify them — the account is in Shuyan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Wuxing, Yang Jiqing and others, rebelled; Luan sent Army Commander Fu Shuyan to suppress them — the account appears in Shuyan's biography.

sentences.zh: 巒之初至漢中，從容風雅，接豪右以禮，撫細民以惠。

translations.literal: When Luan first reached Hanzhong, he was easy and refined, receiving the powerful gentry with courtesy and soothing the common people with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first reached Hanzhong, he was easy and refined, receiving powerful gentry with courtesy and soothing common people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘之後，頗因百姓去就，誅滅齊民，藉為奴婢者二百餘口，兼商販聚歛，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he frequently, according to whether common people stayed or left, executed registered households and seized more than two hundred as slaves; he also traded and amassed wealth — men of clear judgment despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he frequently executed registered households according to whether common people stayed or left, seizing more than two hundred as slaves; he also traded and amassed wealth — men of clear judgment despised him.

sentences.zh: 徵授度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Director of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍遣兵侵軼徐兗，緣邊鎮戍相繼陷沒，朝廷憂之，乃以巒為使持節、都督東討諸軍事、安東將軍，尚書如故。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent troops to raid Xu and Yan; frontier garrisons fell one after another; the court was troubled and appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Eastern Campaign Forces, and General Who Pacifies the East, retaining his rank as Director.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yan sent troops raiding Xu and Yan; frontier garrisons fell in succession; the court was alarmed and appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Eastern Campaign Forces, and General Who Pacifies the East, retaining his directorship.

sentences.zh: 世宗勞遣巒於東堂曰：「蕭衍寇邊，旬朔滋甚，諸軍舛互，規致連戍陷沒。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong saw Luan off with words of encouragement in the Eastern Hall, saying, "Xiao Yan raids the borders; within ten days and a month the harm grows worse; the armies are at cross purposes, planning in ways that cause garrison after garrison to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong saw Luan off with encouragement in the Eastern Hall: "Xiao Yan raids our borders; within weeks the harm grows worse; the armies are at cross purposes, planning in ways that lose garrison after garrison.

sentences.zh: 宋魯之民尤罹湯炭。

translations.literal: The people of Song and Lu suffer especially in fire and boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Song and Lu above all endure fire and boiling water.

sentences.zh: 誠知將軍旋京未久，膝下難違，然東南之寄，非將軍莫可。

translations.literal: I truly know the general has not long returned to the capital and finds it hard to leave his parents' side — yet the trust of the southeast rests on no one but you.
translations.idiomatic: I know well you have not long returned to the capital and find it hard to leave your parents — yet the southeast trusts no one but you.

sentences.zh: 將軍其勉建殊績，以稱朕懷，自古忠臣亦非無孝也。」

translations.literal: General, strive to build exceptional merit to match my hopes — loyal ministers since antiquity have not been without filial feeling."
translations.idiomatic: General, strive for exceptional merit to match my hopes — loyal ministers since antiquity have not lacked filial feeling."

sentences.zh: 巒對曰：「賊雖送死連城，犬羊眾盛，然逆順理殊，滅當無遠。

translations.literal: Luan replied, "Though the enemy rush to their deaths city after city and their barbarian hordes are many, yet the logic of rebellion and submission differs — their destruction cannot be far.
translations.idiomatic: Luan answered, "Though the enemy rush to their deaths city after city and their barbarian hordes are many, the logic of rebellion and submission differs — their destruction cannot be far.

sentences.zh: 況臣仗陛下之神算，奉律以摧之，平殄之期可指辰而待，願陛下勿以東南為慮。」

translations.literal: Moreover your subject relies on Your Majesty's divine strategy and destroys them according to law — the day of total pacification can be awaited by counting the days; I pray Your Majesty not to worry over the southeast."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I rely on Your Majesty's divine strategy and destroy them by law — the day of total pacification can be counted in days; I pray Your Majesty not to worry over the southeast."

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「漢祖有云『金吾擊郾，吾無憂矣』，今將軍董戎，朕何慮哉。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said, "The Han Founder said, 'The Golden Guard strikes Ying — I have no worries' — now the general commands the army; what have I to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said, "The Han Founder said, 'When the Golden Guard strikes Ying, I have no worries' — now you command the army; what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍輔國將軍蕭及先率眾二萬，寇陷固城；

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Xiao Jixian led twenty thousand men and raided and took Gucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Xiao Jixian led twenty thousand men, raided, and took Gucheng;

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍魯顯文、驍騎將軍相文玉等率眾一萬，屯於孤山；

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Xianwen and General of the Valiant Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand men and encamped at Gushan;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Xianwen and General of the Valiant Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand men and camped at Gushan;

sentences.zh: [7]衍將角念等率眾一萬，擾亂龜蒙，土民從逆，十室而五。

translations.literal: [7] Xiao Yan's general Jiao Nian and others led ten thousand men and disturbed Gui and Meng; local people followed the rebellion — five households in ten.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Xiao Yan's general Jiao Nian and others led ten thousand men and disturbed Gui and Meng; local people joined the rebellion — five households in ten.

sentences.zh: 巒遣統軍樊魯討文玉，別將元恒攻固城，統軍畢祖朽討角念。

translations.literal: Luan sent Army Commander Fan Lu to attack Wenyu; another commander Yuan Heng attacked Gucheng; Army Commander Bi Zuxiu attacked Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Luan sent Army Commander Fan Lu against Wenyu; another detachment under Yuan Heng against Gucheng; Army Commander Bi Zuxiu against Nian.

sentences.zh: 樊魯大破文玉等，追奔八十餘里，斬首四千餘級。

translations.literal: Fan Lu greatly defeated Wenyu and the others, pursuing them over eighty li and taking more than four thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Lu routed Wenyu and the others, pursuing over eighty li and taking more than four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 元恒又破固城，畢祖朽復破念等，兗州悉平。

translations.literal: Yuan Heng again broke Gucheng; Bi Zuxiu again defeated Nian and the others — Yan province was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Heng again broke Gucheng; Bi Zuxiu again defeated Nian — Yan province was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 巒破賊將藍懷恭於睢口，進圍宿豫。

translations.literal: Luan defeated the rebel general Lan Huigong at Suikou and advanced to besiege Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan routed the rebel general Lan Huigong at Suikou and advanced to invest Suyu.

sentences.zh: 而懷恭等復於清南造城，[8]規斷水陸之路。

translations.literal: Huigong and the others again built a city at Qingnan [8] planning to cut the water and land routes.
translations.idiomatic: Huigong and the others again built a city at Qingnan [8], planning to sever the water and land routes.

sentences.zh: 巒身率諸軍，自水南而進，遣平南將軍楊大眼從北逼之，統軍劉思祖等夾水造筏，燒其船舫。

translations.literal: Luan personally led the armies forward from the south bank of the water and sent General Who Pacifies the South Yang Dayan to press from the north; Army Commander Liu Sizu and others built rafts on both sides of the water and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Luan personally led the armies forward from the south bank and sent General Who Pacifies the South Yang Dayan to press from the north; Army Commander Liu Sizu and others built rafts on both sides and burned the enemy boats.

sentences.zh: 眾軍齊進，拔柵填塹，登其城。

translations.literal: The armies advanced together, pulling up palisades and filling moats, and scaled the wall.
translations.idiomatic: All armies advanced together, pulling palisades and filling moats, and scaled the wall.

sentences.zh: 火起中流，四面俱擊，仍陷賊城，俘斬數萬。

translations.literal: Fire rose midstream; they struck on four sides and still took the rebel city; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Fire rose midstream; they struck on four sides and took the rebel city; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 在陳別斬懷恭，擒其列侯、列將、直閤、直後三十餘人，俘斬一萬。

translations.literal: At Chen they separately beheaded Huigong and captured more than thirty marquises, generals, Direct Attendants, and Direct Rear Attendants; captives and heads reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen they separately executed Huigong and captured more than thirty marquises, generals, Direct Attendants, and Direct Rear Attendants; captives and heads reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 宿豫既平，蕭昞亦於淮陽退走，二戍獲米四十餘萬石。

translations.literal: With Suyu pacified, Xiao Bing also withdrew from Huaiyang; the two garrisons yielded more than four hundred thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Once Suyu was pacified, Xiao Bing also withdrew from Huaiyang; the two garrisons yielded more than four hundred thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 世宗賜巒璽書曰：「知大龕醜虜，威振賊庭，淮外霧披，徐方卷壒，王略遠恢，混一維始，公私慶泰，何快如之！

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent Luan an imperial letter: "I know the great den of ugly barbarians has been shaken in prestige at the rebel court; beyond the Huai the mist is scattered and Xu is swept clean — the royal strategy extends far and unification begins; public and private rejoice — what joy equals this!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Luan an imperial letter: "I know the great lair of ugly barbarians has shaken the rebel court; beyond the Huai the mist is scattered and Xu swept clean — the royal strategy extends far and unification begins; public and private rejoice — what joy equals this!

sentences.zh: 賊衍此舉，實為傾國。

translations.literal: This move of the rebel Yan truly exhausted the nation.
translations.idiomatic: This move of the rebel Yan truly exhausted his nation.

sentences.zh: 比者宿豫陷歿，淮陽嬰城，凶狡侜張，規抗王旅。

translations.literal: Recently Suyu fell and Huaiyang clung to its walls; the vicious and cunning blustered, planning to resist the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Suyu fell and Huaiyang clung to its walls; the vicious and cunning blustered, planning to resist the royal army.

sentences.zh: 將軍忠規協著，火烈霜摧，電動岱陰，風掃沂嶧，遂令逋誅之寇，一朝殲夷；

translations.literal: The general's loyal plan was jointly manifest; fire scorched and frost shattered; lightning moved at Dai's shadow and wind swept Yi and Yi — thus the long-fugitive bandits were destroyed in a morning;
translations.idiomatic: The general's loyal design shone forth; fire scorched and frost shattered; lightning moved in Dai's shadow and wind swept Yi and Yi — thus long-fugitive bandits were destroyed in a morning;

sentences.zh: 元鯨大憝，千里折首。

translations.literal: the great whale and chief villain had their heads broken a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: the great villain was broken a thousand li away like a beached whale.

sentences.zh: 殊勳茂捷，自古莫二。

translations.literal: Such exceptional merit and splendid victory — since antiquity, none second.
translations.idiomatic: Merit so exceptional and victory so splendid — since antiquity, none its equal.

sentences.zh: 但揚區未安，餘燼宜盪，乘勝掎角，勢不可遺。

translations.literal: But the Yang region is not yet secure; remaining embers should be swept away; pressing the advantage from two sides — momentum must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yang region is not yet secure; remaining embers should be swept; pressing the advantage from two sides — momentum must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 便可率厲三軍，因時經略，申威東南，清彼江介，忘此仍勞，用圖永逸，進退規度，委之高算。」

translations.literal: You may lead and rouse the three armies, seize the moment for strategy, display might in the southeast and clear the river lands; forget present toil for lasting ease — advance and retreat, leave to your high calculation."
translations.idiomatic: Lead and rouse the three armies, seize the moment, display might in the southeast and clear the river lands; forget present toil for lasting ease — advance and retreat, leave to your high calculation."

sentences.zh: 又詔巒曰：「淮陽、宿豫雖已清復，梁城之賊，猶敢聚結，事宜乘勝，并勢摧殄。

translations.literal: Another edict to Luan said, "Though Huaiyang and Suyu are already cleared and recovered, the bandits at Liangcheng still dare gather — the time calls for pressing the advantage and combining momentum to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict to Luan said, "Though Huaiyang and Suyu are cleared, the bandits at Liangcheng still dare gather — the time calls for pressing the advantage and combining momentum to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 可率二萬之眾渡淮，與征南掎角，以圖進取之計。」

translations.literal: Lead twenty thousand men across the Huai, coordinate with the southern expedition in pincer fashion, and plan the advance to take them."
translations.idiomatic: Lead twenty thousand men across the Huai, coordinate with the southern expedition in pincer fashion, and plan the advance."

sentences.zh: 及梁城賊走，中山王英乘勝攻鍾離，又詔巒帥眾會之。

translations.literal: When the bandits at Liangcheng fled, Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pressed the advantage to attack Zhongli; another edict ordered Luan to lead his troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits at Liangcheng fled, Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pressed the advantage against Zhongli; another edict ordered Luan to lead his troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 巒表曰：「奉被詔旨，令臣濟淮與征南掎角，乘勝長驅，實是其會。

translations.literal: Luan submitted a memorial: "Obeying the edict to cross the Huai and coordinate with the southern expedition in pincer fashion, pressing the advantage in long pursuit — truly this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized: "Obeying the edict to cross the Huai and coordinate with the southern expedition, pressing the advantage in long pursuit — truly this is the moment.

sentences.zh: 但愚懷所量，竊有未盡。

translations.literal: But what my foolish heart measures, I privately find incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: But what my foolish heart measures, I find incomplete.

sentences.zh: 夫圖南因於積風，伐國在於資給，用兵治戎，須先計校。

translations.literal: Plans for the south depend on accumulated wind; conquering a state depends on supplies; using troops and governing the army — one must first calculate.
translations.idiomatic: Plans for the south depend on accumulated wind; conquering a state depends on supplies; using troops — one must first calculate.

sentences.zh: 非可抑為必勝，[9]幸其無能。

translations.literal: One cannot suppress this into certain victory [9] and rely on their incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot simply assume certain victory [9] and count on their incompetence.

sentences.zh: 若欲掠地誅民，必應萬勝；

translations.literal: If one wishes to seize land and punish the people, ten thousand victories are required;
translations.idiomatic: To seize land and punish the people requires ten thousand victories;

sentences.zh: 如欲攻城取邑，未見其果。

translations.literal: if one wishes to storm cities and take towns, the outcome is not yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes to storm cities and take towns, success is not yet assured.

sentences.zh: 得之則所益未幾，不獲則虧損必大。

translations.literal: If gained, the benefit is slight; if not gained, the loss is sure to be great.
translations.idiomatic: If gained, the benefit is slight; if not, the loss is sure to be great.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍傾竭江東，為今歲之舉，疲兵喪眾，大敗而還，君臣失計，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan exhausted the lands east of the Yang for this year's campaign; his troops are weary and his masses lost — a great defeat and return; ruler and ministers lost their plan and became the world's laughingstock.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan exhausted the lands east of the Yang for this year's campaign; his troops are weary and his masses lost — a great defeat; ruler and ministers lost their plan and became the world's laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 雖野戰非人敵，守城足有餘，今雖攻之，未易可克。

translations.literal: Though they are no match in field battle, for holding cities they more than suffice; though we attack now, it is not easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Though no match in field battle, for holding cities they more than suffice; attacked now, they are not easily taken.

sentences.zh: 又廣陵懸遠，去江四十里，鍾離、淮陰介在淮外，假其歸順而來，猶恐無糧艱守，況加攻討，勞兵士乎？

translations.literal: Moreover Guangling hangs far away, forty li from the Yang; Zhongli and Huaiyin lie beyond the Huai — even if they came in submission, I still fear holding them without grain would be hard; how much more if we add assault and weary the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guangling hangs far away, forty li from the Yang; Zhongli and Huaiyin lie beyond the Huai — even if they submitted, holding them without grain would be hard; how much more if we add assault and weary the soldiers?

sentences.zh: 且征南軍士從戎二時，疲弊死病，量可知已。

translations.literal: Moreover the southern expedition's soldiers have been at war two seasons; weariness, death, and sickness — the measure is known.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the southern expedition's soldiers have campaigned two seasons; weariness, death, and sickness — the measure is known.

sentences.zh: 雖有乘勝之資，懼無遠用之力。

translations.literal: Though there is momentum for victory, I fear there is not strength for distant use.
translations.idiomatic: Though victory's momentum is ours, I fear we lack strength for distant operations.

sentences.zh: 若臣之愚見，謂宜修復舊戍，牢實邊方，息養中州，擬之後舉。

translations.literal: If my foolish view, we should restore the old garrisons, solidify the borders, rest and nurture the Central Provinces, and plan for a later campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, we should restore the old garrisons, solidify the borders, rest the Central Provinces, and plan a later campaign.

sentences.zh: 又江東之釁，不患久無，畜力待機，謂為勝計。」

translations.literal: Moreover the trouble east of the Yang — I do not worry it will long be absent; storing strength and awaiting the moment is, I say, the winning plan."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover trouble east of the Yang will not long be absent; storing strength and awaiting the moment is the winning plan."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「濟淮掎角，事如前敕，何容猶爾磐桓，方有此請！

translations.literal: An edict said, "Cross the Huai in pincer fashion — the affair is as in the earlier edict; how can you still hesitate and make this request!
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Cross the Huai in pincer fashion — as in the earlier edict; how can you still hesitate and make this request!

sentences.zh: 可速進軍，經略之宜聽征南至要。」

translations.literal: Advance the army swiftly; strategic matters — heed the southern expedition's essentials."
translations.idiomatic: Advance swiftly; strategic matters — heed the southern expedition's essentials."

sentences.zh: 巒又表曰：「蕭衍侵境，久勞王師，今者奔走，實除邊患，斯由靈贊皇魏，天敗寇豎，非臣等弱劣所能克勝。

translations.literal: Luan submitted another memorial: "Xiao Yan invaded the borders and long wearied the royal army; now they flee — truly removing the frontier trouble — this is by the numinous favor of great Wei and heaven's defeat of the rebel bandits, not because your subjects' weakness could overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again: "Xiao Yan invaded the borders and long wearied the royal army; now they flee — truly removing frontier trouble — by the numinous favor of great Wei and heaven's defeat of the rebels, not because we weaklings overcame them.

sentences.zh: 若臣之愚見，今正宜修復邊鎮，俟之後動。

translations.literal: If my foolish view, now is precisely the time to restore the frontier garrisons and wait for later action.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, now is precisely the time to restore frontier garrisons and wait.

sentences.zh: 且蕭衍尚在，凶身未除，螳蜋之志，何能自息。

translations.literal: Moreover Xiao Yan still lives and his vicious person is not removed — the mantis's ambition, how can it rest of itself?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xiao Yan still lives and his vicious self is not removed — the mantis's ambition, how can it rest?

sentences.zh: 唯應廣備以待其來，實不宜勞師遠入，自取疲困。

translations.literal: We should only prepare broadly and await his coming — truly we should not weary the army with distant entry and bring exhaustion on ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We should only prepare broadly and await his coming — not weary the army with distant entry and bring exhaustion on ourselves.

sentences.zh: 今中山進軍鍾離，實所未解，若能為得失之計，不顧萬全，直襲廣陵，入其內地，出其不備，或未可知。

translations.literal: Now Prince of Zhongshan advances on Zhongli — truly I do not understand it; if he can weigh gain and loss, disregard complete safety, and strike directly at Guangling into their interior, catching them unprepared — perhaps something may be unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Zhongshan advances on Zhongli — I do not understand it; if he can weigh gain and loss, disregard complete safety, strike directly at Guangling into their interior, catching them unprepared — perhaps something may come of it.

sentences.zh: 正欲屯兵，蕭密餘軍猶自在彼；

translations.literal: Just as he means to encamp, Xiao Yan's remaining troops are still there;
translations.idiomatic: Just when he intends to encamp, Xiao Yan's remaining troops are still there;

sentences.zh: 欲言無糧，運船復至。

translations.literal: if one says there is no grain, supply ships arrive again.
translations.idiomatic: say there is no grain, and supply ships arrive again.

sentences.zh: 而欲以八十日糧圖城者，臣未之前聞。

translations.literal: Yet to plan taking a city with eighty days' grain — your subject has never heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to plan taking a city with eighty days' grain — I have never heard of it.

sentences.zh: 且廣陵、任城可為前戒，豈容今者復欲同之。

translations.literal: Moreover Guangling and Rencheng can serve as prior warning — how can we now wish to do the same again?
translations.idiomatic: Guangling and Rencheng serve as prior warning — how can we wish to do the same again?

sentences.zh: 今若往也，彼牢城自守，不與人戰，城壍水深，非可填塞，空坐至春，則士自弊苦。

translations.literal: If we go now, they will hold the strong city and not give battle; the moat is deep and cannot be filled — sitting idle until spring, the soldiers will weary of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If we go now, they will hold the strong city and refuse battle; the moat is deep and cannot be filled — sitting idle until spring, the soldiers will wear themselves out.

sentences.zh: 遣臣赴彼，糧何以致？

translations.literal: Send your subject there — how will grain arrive?
translations.idiomatic: Send me there — how will grain arrive?

sentences.zh: 夏來之兵，不齎冬服，脫遇冰雪，取濟何方？

translations.literal: Soldiers coming in summer carry no winter clothing — if they meet ice and snow, where will relief come?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers coming in summer carry no winter clothing — if they meet ice and snow, where will relief come from?

sentences.zh: 臣寧荷怯懦不進之責，不受敗損空行之罪。

translations.literal: Your subject would rather bear the charge of timidity and not advancing than accept the crime of defeat and empty marching.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather bear the charge of timidity and not advancing than accept the crime of defeat and empty marching.

sentences.zh: 鍾離天險，朝貴所具，若有內應，則所不知，如其無也，必無克狀。

translations.literal: Zhongli is heaven's barrier — the court nobles know this; if there is collusion within, that I do not know; if not, there is surely no prospect of success.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli is heaven's barrier — the court nobles know it; if there is collusion within, I do not know; if not, success is surely impossible.

sentences.zh: 若其不復，其辱如何！

translations.literal: If it is not recovered, what shame will there be!
translations.idiomatic: If it is not recovered, what disgrace will follow!

sentences.zh: 若信臣言也，願賜臣停；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty trusts my words, I beg to be granted a halt;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty trusts my words, I beg permission to halt;

sentences.zh: 若謂臣難行求回，臣所領兵統悉付中山，任其處分，臣求單騎隨逐東西。

translations.literal: if you say I find the march hard and seek return, all troops under my command I hand over to Prince of Zhongshan for his disposal; I ask to follow east and west with a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: if you say I find the march hard and seek return, all troops under my command I hand to Prince of Zhongshan; I ask to follow with a single horse.

sentences.zh: 且俗諺云，耕則問田奴，絹則問織婢。

translations.literal: Moreover the common saying goes: for plowing ask the field slave; for silk ask the weaving maid.
translations.idiomatic: The common saying goes: for plowing ask the field slave; for silk ask the weaving maid.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不武，忝備征將，前宜可否，頗實知之，臣既謂難，何容強遣。」

translations.literal: Your subject, though not martial, disgracefully holds the rank of campaign general; of what should precede and what should not, I truly know — since I say it is hard, how can I be forced to go?
translations.idiomatic: I, though not martial, disgracefully hold the rank of campaign general; of what should precede and what should not, I truly know — since I say it is hard, how can I be forced to go?

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「安東頻請罷軍，遲回未往，阻異戎規，殊乖至望。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The Pacifier of the East repeatedly requests to halt the army, delays and has not gone, obstructing the military plan — greatly contrary to utmost expectation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The Pacifier of the East repeatedly requests to halt, delays and has not gone, obstructing the military plan — greatly contrary to expectation.

sentences.zh: 士馬既殷，無容停積，宜務神速，東西齊契，乘勝掃殄，以赴機會。」

translations.literal: Soldiers and horses are abundant — there is no room for delay; strive for swiftness; east and west in accord; press the advantage and sweep clean to seize the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and horses are abundant — no room for delay; strive for swiftness; east and west in accord; press the advantage to seize the moment."

sentences.zh: 巒累表求還，世宗許之。

translations.literal: Luan repeatedly memorialized asking to return; Emperor Shizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan repeatedly petitioned to return; Emperor Shizong granted his request.

sentences.zh: 英果敗退，時人伏其識略。

translations.literal: Ying indeed was defeated and withdrew; men of the time admired Luan's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was indeed defeated and withdrew; men of the time admired Luan's foresight.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中盧昶與巒不平，昶與元暉俱世宗所寵，御史中尉崔亮，昶之黨也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang was on bad terms with Luan; Chang and Yuan Hui were both favorites of Emperor Shizong; Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang was Chang's partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang was on bad terms with Luan; Chang and Yuan Hui were both favorites of Emperor Shizong; Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang was Chang's ally.

sentences.zh: 昶、暉令亮糾巒，事成許言於世宗以亮為侍中。

translations.literal: Chang and Hui had Liang impeach Luan, promising that if it succeeded they would speak to Emperor Shizong to make Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Hui had Liang impeach Luan, promising that if the case succeeded they would speak to Emperor Shizong to make Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 亮於是奏劾巒在漢中掠良人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon memorialized impeaching Luan for seizing registered commoners as slaves in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then memorialized, accusing Luan of seizing registered commoners as slaves in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巒懼為昶等所陷，乃以漢中所得巴西太守龐景民女化生等二十餘口與暉。

translations.literal: Luan feared being trapped by Chang and the others and therefore gave Hui more than twenty persons taken in Hanzhong, including Huasheng, daughter of Baxi Administrator Pang Jingmin.
translations.idiomatic: Luan feared being trapped by Chang and the others and gave Hui more than twenty persons taken in Hanzhong, including Huasheng, daughter of Baxi Administrator Pang Jingmin.

sentences.zh: 化生等數人，奇色也，暉大悅，乃背昶為巒言於世宗云：「巒新有大功，已經赦宥，不宜方為此獄也。」

translations.literal: Huasheng and several others were of extraordinary beauty; Hui was greatly pleased and therefore turned against Chang and spoke for Luan to Emperor Shizong, saying, "Luan has lately achieved great merit and has already been pardoned — he should not now be put through this prosecution."
translations.idiomatic: Huasheng and several others were of extraordinary beauty; Hui was greatly pleased, turned against Chang, and spoke for Luan to Emperor Shizong: "Luan has lately achieved great merit and has already been pardoned — he should not now face this prosecution."

sentences.zh: 世宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 高肇以巒有克敵之效，而為昶等所排，助巒申釋，故得不坐。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, because Luan had the effect of defeating the enemy yet was pushed aside by Chang and the others, helped Luan plead his case, and therefore he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, because Luan had defeated the enemy yet was pushed aside by Chang and the others, helped plead his case, and therefore he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 豫州城民白早生殺刺史司馬悅，以城南入，蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍齊苟仁率眾入據懸瓠。

translations.literal: The city people of Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, killed Governor Sima Yue and submitted the south of the city; Xiao Yan sent his General Who Conquers the Enemy Qi Gouren leading troops to enter and hold Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: The city people of Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, killed Governor Sima Yue and submitted the south of the city; Xiao Yan sent his General Who Conquers the Enemy Qi Gouren with troops to enter and hold Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 詔巒持節率羽林精騎以討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Luan to bear the staff and lead picked cavalry of the Feathered Forest to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Luan to bear the staff and lead picked Feathered Forest cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 封平舒縣開國伯，食邑五百戶，賞宿豫之功也。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingshu District with a fief of five hundred households — reward for the merit at Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingshu District with a fief of five hundred households — reward for the victory at Suyu.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨東堂，勞遣巒曰：「司馬悅不慎重門之戒，智不足以謀身，匪直喪元隸豎，[11]乃大虧王略。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall and saw him off with encouragement, saying, "Sima Yue did not heed the warning of the heavy gate; his wisdom was insufficient to preserve himself — not only did he lose his head to the villain, [11] he greatly harmed the royal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall and saw him off: "Sima Yue ignored the warning of the heavy gate; his wisdom could not preserve him — not only did he lose his head to the villain, [11] he greatly harmed the royal strategy.

sentences.zh: 懸瓠密邇近畿，東南藩捍，度公之在彼，[12]憂慮尤深。

translations.literal: Xuanhu lies close to the near capital, the southeastern bulwark — considering that you will be there, [12] the worry is especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhu lies close to the near capital, the southeastern bulwark — knowing you will be there, [12] my worry is especially deep.
