sentences.zh: 早生理不獨立，必遠引吳楚，士民同惡，勢或交兵。

translations.literal: If Zaosheng cannot stand alone, he will surely draw Wu and Chu from afar; gentry and people share the hatred — force may join in battle.
translations.idiomatic: If Zaosheng cannot stand alone, he will surely draw Wu and Chu from afar; gentry and people share the hatred — battle may join.

sentences.zh: 卿文昭武烈，朝之南仲，故令卿星言電邁，出其不意。

translations.literal: You combine literary brilliance and martial valor — the court's Nan Zhong; therefore I order you to move like a star, swift as lightning, and catch them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: You combine literary brilliance and martial valor — the court's Nan Zhong; therefore I order you to move like a star, swift as lightning, catching them unprepared.

sentences.zh: 卿言早生走也守也？

translations.literal: Do you say Zaosheng will flee or hold?
translations.idiomatic: Will Zaosheng flee or hold?

sentences.zh: 何時可以平之？」

translations.literal: When can he be pacified?
translations.idiomatic: When can the region be pacified?

sentences.zh: 巒對曰：「早生非有深謀大智能構成此也，但因司馬悅虐於百姓，乘眾怒而為之，民為凶威所懾，不得已而苟附。

translations.literal: Luan replied, "Zaosheng has no deep plan or great wisdom capable of bringing this about — he acted only because Sima Yue was cruel to the common people and he rode the crowd's anger; the people, awed by his vicious might, joined him unwillingly and for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Luan answered, "Zaosheng has no deep plan or great wisdom to bring this about — he acted because Sima Yue was cruel to the people and he rode popular anger; the people, awed by his vicious might, joined unwillingly for the moment.

sentences.zh: 假蕭衍軍入應，水路不通，糧運不繼，亦成擒耳，不能為害也。

translations.literal: Even if Xiao Yan's army enters to support him, the water route is blocked and grain transport cannot continue — he becomes something already captured and cannot do harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiao Yan's army enters to support him, the water route is blocked and grain cannot follow — he becomes prey in hand and cannot harm us.

sentences.zh: 早生得衍軍之接，溺於利欲之情，必守而不走。

translations.literal: Zaosheng, receiving Xiao Yan's army's aid, drowned in desire for profit — he is sure to hold and not flee.
translations.idiomatic: Zaosheng, receiving Xiao Yan's support, drowned in greed — he is sure to hold and not flee.

sentences.zh: 今王師若臨，士民必翻然歸順。

translations.literal: If the royal army now arrives, gentry and people will surely turn and submit.
translations.idiomatic: If the royal army arrives now, gentry and people will surely turn and submit.

sentences.zh: 圍之窮城，奔走路絕，不度此年，必傳首京師。

translations.literal: Besieged in a desperate city with flight cut off, before this year ends his head will surely reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged in a desperate city with flight cut off, before this year ends his head will reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 願陛下不足垂慮。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty need not worry overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty need not worry."

sentences.zh: 世宗笑曰：「卿言何其壯哉！

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong smiled and said, "How bold your words!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong smiled: "How bold your words!

sentences.zh: 深會朕遣卿之意。

translations.literal: You deeply grasp my intent in sending you.
translations.idiomatic: You fully grasp why I am sending you.

sentences.zh: 知卿親老，頻勞於外，然忠孝不俱，才宜救世，不得辭也。」

translations.literal: I know your parents are aged and you are frequently wearied abroad — yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled; talent should save the age — you cannot decline."
translations.idiomatic: I know your parents are aged and you are frequently wearied abroad — yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled; talent should save the age — you may not decline."

sentences.zh: 於是巒率騎八百，倍道兼行，五日次於鮑口。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luan led eight hundred cavalry, traveling day and night, and on the fifth day halted at Baokou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Luan led eight hundred cavalry by forced marches and on the fifth day halted at Baokou.

sentences.zh: 賊遣大將軍胡孝智率眾七千，去城二百，逆來拒戰。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Grand General Hu Xiaozhi leading seven thousand men two hundred li from the city to come out and oppose.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Grand General Hu Xiaozhi with seven thousand men two hundred li from the city to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 巒擊破孝智，乘勝長驅，至於懸瓠。

translations.literal: Luan defeated Xiaozhi and pressed the victory in long pursuit to Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan defeated Xiaozhi and pressed the pursuit to Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 賊出城逆戰，又大破之，因即渡汝。

translations.literal: The rebels came out to oppose and were again greatly defeated; he thereupon crossed the Ru.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to fight and were again routed; he thereupon crossed the Ru.

sentences.zh: 既而大兵繼至，遂長圍之。

translations.literal: Soon the main army followed and a long siege was established.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main army arrived and a long siege was established.

sentences.zh: 詔加巒使持節、假鎮南將軍、都督南討諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict added to Luan's commission: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Provisional General Who Pacifies the South, and Commander-in-Chief of All Southern Campaign Forces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further invested Luan as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Provisional General Who Pacifies the South, and Commander-in-Chief of All Southern Campaign Forces.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍、中山王英南討三關，亦次於懸瓠，以後軍未至，前寇稍多，憚不敢進，乃與巒分兵掎角攻之。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying campaigned south against the Three Passes and also halted at Xuanhu; because the rear army had not arrived and bandits ahead were somewhat numerous, he feared and dared not advance — he and Luan divided forces in pincer fashion to attack.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the South Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying campaigned south against the Three Passes and also halted at Xuanhu; because the rear army had not arrived and enemies ahead were numerous, he feared and dared not advance — he and Luan divided forces in pincer fashion.

sentences.zh: 衍將齊苟仁等二十一人開門出降，即斬早生等同惡數十人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's generals Qi Gouren and twenty others opened the gate and came out to surrender; they immediately beheaded Zaosheng and several dozen fellow evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's generals Qi Gouren and twenty others opened the gate and surrendered; they immediately beheaded Zaosheng and several dozen fellow evildoers.

sentences.zh: 豫州平，巒振旅還京師。

translations.literal: Yuzhou pacified, Luan led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuzhou pacified, Luan led the army back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨東堂勞之，曰：「卿役不踰時，克清妖醜，鴻勳碩美，可謂無愧古人。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall with encouragement, saying, "Your service did not exceed the season yet you cleared away the evil — splendid merit, truly without shame before the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall: "Your service did not exceed the season yet you cleared away evil — splendid merit, without shame before the ancients.

sentences.zh: 巒對曰：「此自陛下聖略威靈，英等將士之力，臣何功之有。」

translations.literal: Luan replied, "This is by Your Majesty's sacred strategy and awesome spirit and the strength of Prince Ying and the officers and soldiers — what merit has your subject?"
translations.idiomatic: Luan answered, "This is by Your Majesty's sacred strategy and the strength of Prince Ying and the officers — what merit have I?"

sentences.zh: 世宗笑曰：「卿匪直一月三捷，所足稱奇，乃存士伯，欲功成而不處。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong smiled and said, "You are not merely remarkable for three victories in one month — you also preserve the manner of a gentleman, wishing merit accomplished yet not claiming it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong smiled: "You are not merely remarkable for three victories in one month — you preserve the manner of a gentleman, wishing merit done yet not claiming it."

sentences.zh: 巒自宿豫大捷，及平懸瓠，志行修正，不復以財賄為懷，戎資軍實絲毫無犯。

translations.literal: From the great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xuanhu, Luan's conduct and aims were corrected; he no longer harbored bribery in his heart, and military funds and stores he did not violate in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: From the great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xuanhu, Luan corrected his conduct; he no longer sought bribes, and military funds and stores he did not touch in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，暴疾卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yan chang he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yan chang he died suddenly of illness at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 巒才兼文武，朝野瞻望，上下悼惜之。

translations.literal: Luan combined civil and military talent; court and country looked up to him; above and below mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Luan combined civil and military talent; court and country looked up to him; all mourned him.

sentences.zh: 詔賻帛四百匹，朝服一襲，贈車騎大將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict granted four hundred bolts of silk, one set of court robes, and posthumously awarded Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted four hundred bolts of silk and one set of court robes, and posthumously honored him as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗欲贈冀州，黃門甄琛以巒前曾劾己，乃云：「瀛州巒之本邦，人情所欲。」

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Shizong wished to award Jizhou; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhen Chen, because Luan had once impeached him, said, "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery — that is what popular sentiment desires."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Shizong wished to award Jizhou; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhen Chen, because Luan had once impeached him, said, "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery — that is what people wish."

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: He followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 及琛為詔，乃云「優贈車騎將軍、瀛州刺史」，議者笑琛淺薄。

translations.literal: When Chen drafted the edict he wrote "posthumously awarded with special honor Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou" — commentators laughed at Chen's pettiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote only "posthumously awarded with special honor Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yingzhou" — onlookers laughed at Chen's pettiness.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Wendin.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous epithet: Wendin.

sentences.zh: 子遜，字子言。

translations.literal: His son Xun, courtesy name Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, styled Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 貌雖陋短，頗有風氣。

translations.literal: Though his appearance was ugly and he was short, he had considerable spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Though ugly and short in stature, he had considerable spirit.

sentences.zh: 解褐司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first office he was appointed Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first office he was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 襲爵。

translations.literal: He inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 後遷國子博士、本州中正。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Doctor of the Imperial University and Grand Coordinator of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Doctor of the Imperial University and Grand Coordinator of his native province.

sentences.zh: 因謁靈太后，自陳：「功名之子，久抱沉屈。

translations.literal: On audience with Empress Dowager Ling he stated himself: "The son of a man of merit long bears hidden grievance.
translations.idiomatic: On audience with Empress Dowager Ling he stated: "The son of a man of merit long bears hidden grievance.

sentences.zh: 臣父屢為大將，而臣身無軍功階級，臣父唯為忠臣，不為慈父。」

translations.literal: My father repeatedly served as grand general yet I myself have no military merit or rank; my father was only a loyal minister, not a loving father."
translations.idiomatic: My father repeatedly served as grand general yet I have no military merit or rank; my father was only a loyal minister, not a loving father."

sentences.zh: 靈太后慨然，以遜為長兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was moved and appointed Xun Senior Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was moved and made Xun Senior Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為安遠將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Ping province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Ping province.

sentences.zh: 時北蕃多難，稽留不進，免。

translations.literal: At that time the northern frontier had many troubles; he delayed and did not advance — and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the northern frontier had many troubles; he delayed and did not advance and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除輔國將軍、通直散騎常侍、東道軍司，討逆賊劉舉於濮陽，不克。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed General Who Assists the State, Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Eastern Route Army Commander, campaigning against the rebel Liu Ju at Puyang — he did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed General Who Assists the State, Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Eastern Route Army Commander against the rebel Liu Ju at Puyang — he did not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 還，除散騎常侍，加前將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary with the additional title Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary with the additional rank of Forward General.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，坐受任元顥，除名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong an he was punished for accepting appointment under Yuan Hao and was removed from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong an he was punished for accepting appointment under Yuan Hao and was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 尋除撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，轉衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu he was transferred to General of the Guard and Grand Master of the Right Gold Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was transferred to General of the Guard and Grand Master of the Right Gold Seal and Purple Cord.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，以本官領嘗藥典御，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he held his former office and headed the Office of Imperial Pharmacy, with the additional title General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he retained his former office and headed the Office of Imperial Pharmacy, with the additional rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 久之，除大司農卿，與少卿馬慶哲至相糾訟。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture and mutually impeached the Vice Minister Ma Qingzhe in lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture and mutually impeached Vice Minister Ma Qingzhe in lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 遜銳於財利，議者鄙之。

translations.literal: Xun was sharp in pursuit of profit — commentators despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was sharp in pursuit of profit — men of judgment despised him.

sentences.zh: 武定四年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuding he died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、光祿勳卿、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded his former general's rank, Minister of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Governor of You province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored with his former general's rank, Minister of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Governor of You province.

sentences.zh: 子祖微，開府祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Zuwai, Staff Officer of the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuwai served as Staff Officer of the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 父喪未終，謀反，伏法。

translations.literal: Before his father's mourning was ended he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before his father's mourning period had ended he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 巒弟儒，瀛州鎮遠府長史、給事中。

translations.literal: Luan's younger brother Ru, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Distance Office of Ying province and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Ru was Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Distance Office of Ying province and Attendant.

sentences.zh: 儒弟偉，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: Ru's younger brother Wei, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's younger brother Wei was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈博陵太守。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously awarded Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 子昕，在文苑傳。

translations.literal: His son Xin — the account is in the Literary Garden biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin — the account appears in the Literary Garden biography.

sentences.zh: 偉弟季彥。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Jiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan was Wei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 季彥弟晏，字幼平。

translations.literal: Jiyan's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Youping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan's younger brother Yan, styled Youping.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，博涉經史，善談釋老，雅好文詠。

translations.literal: Fine bearing and manner; broad learning in the classics and histories; skilled in discussing Buddhism and Daoism; he loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Fine bearing; broad learning in classics and histories; skilled in discussing Buddhism and Daoism; he loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 起家太學博士、司徒東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: Upon first office he was Doctor of the Imperial University and Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Doctor of the Imperial University and Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為與廣平王懷遊宴，左遷鄚縣令，未之官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he joined Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai in feasting and pleasure and was demoted to Magistrate of Mo county — he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he joined Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai in feasting and was demoted to Magistrate of Mo county — he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 除給事中，遷司空主簿、本州中正、汝南王文學。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant, promoted to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Grand Coordinator of his native province, and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant, then Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Grand Coordinator of his native province, and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、司空長史、兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to General Who Assists the State, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍出為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: With his former general's rank he went out as Governor of Southern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his general's rank, he went out to govern Southern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 徵為太中大夫、兼丞相高陽王右長史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace and Concurrent Right Chief Clerk to the Prince of Gaoyang, Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace and Concurrent Right Chief Clerk to Prince of Gaoyang, Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋以本將軍除滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon with his former general's rank he was appointed Governor of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his general's rank, he was appointed Governor of Cang province.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，吏民安之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and quiet; officials and people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was clear and quiet; officials and people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: He died in the Xiaochang era, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xiaochang era at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈征北將軍、尚書左僕射、瀛州刺史，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the North, Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, Governor of Yingzhou — posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the North, Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Yingzhou — posthumous epithet Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 晏篤於義讓，初為南兗州刺史，例得一子解褐，乃啟其孤弟子子慎，年甫十二，而其子已弱冠矣。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply devoted to righteous yielding; when he first became Governor of Southern Yan province, by precedent one son could enter first office — he petitioned for his orphaned nephew Zishen, just twelve, though his own son was already of mature age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply devoted to righteous yielding; when he first became Governor of Southern Yan, by precedent one son could enter first office — he petitioned for his orphaned nephew Zishen, just twelve, though his own son was already grown.

sentences.zh: 後為滄州，復啟孤兄子昕為府主簿，而其子並未從官。

translations.literal: Later as Governor of Cang he again petitioned for his orphaned elder brother's son Xin as Chief Clerk of the prefecture, while his own sons had not yet held office.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Governor of Cang he again petitioned for his orphaned elder brother's son Xin as prefectural chief clerk, while his own sons had not yet held office.

sentences.zh: 世人以此多之。

translations.literal: Men of the age praised him greatly for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him greatly for this.

sentences.zh: 子測，武定末，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Ce, at the end of Wuding, was Crown Prince's Reader.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ce served as Crown Prince's Reader at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 測弟亢，字子高，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Ce's younger brother Kang, courtesy name Zigao, had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's younger brother Kang, styled Zigao, had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 釋褐司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first office he was Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first office he was clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷廣平王開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Retainer in the Prince of Guangping's Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Retainer in Prince of Guangping's Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 兼通直散騎常侍，使於蕭衍，時年二十八。

translations.literal: Concurrently Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was sent on a mission to Xiao Yan at age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Serving concurrently as Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was sent on a mission to Xiao Yan at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 還，除平東將軍，齊文襄王大將軍府屬，又轉中外府屬。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, staff member in Grand General Qi Wenxiang's office, then transferred to staff of the Central and Outer Office.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, staff member in Grand General Qi Wenxiang's office, then transferred to the Central and Outer Office.

sentences.zh: 武定七年，坐事死於晉陽，年三十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding he was executed at Jinyang for an offense, aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding he was executed at Jinyang for a crime, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 巒叔祖祐，字宗祐。

translations.literal: Luan's granduncle You, courtesy name Zongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's granduncle You, styled Zongyou.

sentences.zh: 少有學尚，知名於時。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and won renown in his time.

sentences.zh: 徵除著作郎，領樂浪王傅。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library and Tutor to the Prince of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned and made Gentleman of the Palace Library and Tutor to the Prince of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 後假員外散騎常侍，使於劉彧。

translations.literal: Later provisionally Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, sent on a mission to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, provisionally Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was sent on a mission to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 以將命之勤，除建威將軍、平原太守，賜爵城平男。

translations.literal: For diligence in carrying out orders he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Pingyuan, and awarded the title Baron of Chengping.
translations.idiomatic: For diligence in carrying out orders he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Pingyuan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chengping.

sentences.zh: 政清刑肅，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and punishments strict; the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was clear and punishments strict; the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: When he died he was aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子產，字神寶。

translations.literal: His son Chan, courtesy name Shenbao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan, styled Shenbao.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 少時作孤蓬賦，為時所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he composed the Rhapsody on the Lone Thistle, praised in its time.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he wrote the Rhapsody on the Lone Thistle, which won praise in its day.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as Cultivated Talent, he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Cultivated Talent, he became Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 假員外常侍、鄚縣子，使於蕭賾。

translations.literal: Provisionally Supernumerary Regular Attendant, Baron of Mo District, sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Provisionally Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Baron of Mo District, sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 產仍世將命，時人美之。

translations.literal: Chan for generations carried out missions — men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family carried out missions — men of the time praised Chan.

sentences.zh: 後遷中書侍郎，俄遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, then soon promoted to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, then soon to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六，朝廷嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: When he died he was aged forty-six; court and country sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged forty-six; court and country sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 贈建威將軍、平州刺史、樂城子，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Ping province, Baron of Lecheng — posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Ping province, and Baron of Lecheng — posthumous epithet Ding.

sentences.zh: 祐從子虬，字神虎。

translations.literal: You's nephew's son Qiu, courtesy name Shenhu.
translations.idiomatic: You's nephew's son Qiu, styled Shenhu.

sentences.zh: 少為三禮鄭氏學，明經有文思。

translations.literal: From youth he studied the Zheng school of the Three Rites, was versed in the classics, and had literary thought.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied the Zheng school of the Three Rites, was versed in the classics, and had literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才上第，為中書議郎、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as Cultivated Talent with highest rank, he was appointed Gentleman Consultant of the Secretariat and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Cultivated Talent with highest rank, he became Gentleman Consultant of the Secretariat and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖因公事與語，問朝覲宴饗之禮，虬以經對，大合上旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu on public business conversed with him and asked about the rites of court audience and banquets; Qiu answered according to the classics — greatly matching the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu on public business conversed with him and asked about court audience and banquet rites; Qiu answered from the classics — greatly matching imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒屬、國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Staff Member of the Ministry of Works and Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the staff of the Ministry of Works and became Doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，尚書令王肅多用新儀，虬往往折以五經正禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died, Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Su often used new rites; Qiu frequently corrected them with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu died, Director Wang Su often used new rites; Qiu frequently corrected them with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書右丞，徙左丞，多所糾正，臺閣肅然。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Director of the Masters of Writing, then moved to Left Director; he corrected much and the secretariat grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Director of the Masters of Writing, then Left Director; he corrected much and the secretariat grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 時雁門人有害母者，八座奏轘之而潴其室，宥其二子。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Yanmen harmed his mother; the Eight Ministers memorialized to dismember him by chariot and impound his house, pardoning his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man of Yanmen killed his mother; the Eight Ministers memorialized to dismember him by chariot and impound his house, pardoning his two sons.

sentences.zh: 虬駁奏云：「君親無將，將而必誅。

translations.literal: Qiu rebutted the memorial, saying, "Ruler and parent must not be plotted against — plot and you are surely executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu rebutted the memorial: "Ruler and parent must not be plotted against — plot and you are surely executed.

sentences.zh: 今謀逆者戮及期親，害親者今不及子，既逆甚梟鏡，禽獸之不若，而使禋祀不絕，遺育永傳，非所以勸忠孝之道，存三綱之義。

translations.literal: Now those who plot rebellion are executed to the end of their close kin; those who harm kin are not punished to the sons — this inverts the severity of the owl and mirror; worse than beasts — yet sacrificial rites are not cut off and descendants perpetually transmitted; this is not the way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or preserve the three bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebels are executed to close kin, yet parricides' sons go unpunished — this inverts the severity owed the owl and mirror, worse than beasts — yet sacrificial rites continue and descendants perpetually transmit; this is not the way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or preserve the three bonds.

sentences.zh: 若聖教含容，不加孥戮，使父子罪不相及，惡止於其身，不則宜投之四裔，敕所在不聽配匹。

translations.literal: If sage teaching is inclusive and does not extend punishment to wives and children, so that father and son crimes do not reach each other and evil stops with the person — otherwise they should be cast to the four wilds and orders issued that none in the land may give them spouses.
translations.idiomatic: If sage teaching is inclusive and does not extend punishment to wives and children, so father and son crimes do not reach each other and evil stops with the person — otherwise cast them to the four wilds and forbid the land to give them spouses.

sentences.zh: 盤庚言『無令易種於新邑』，漢法五月食梟羹，皆欲絕其類也。」

translations.literal: Pan Geng said, 'Do not let a different seed be planted in the new city'; Han law served owl broth in the fifth month — all wished to cut off their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Geng said, 'Do not let a different seed be planted in the new city'; Han law served owl broth in the fifth month — both sought to cut off their kind.

sentences.zh: 奏入，世宗從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Emperor Shizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, Emperor Shizong approved it.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒右長史，遷龍驤將軍、光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, promoted to General of the Flying Dragon and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, then General of the Flying Dragon and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 虬母在鄉遇患，請假歸。

translations.literal: Qiu's mother fell ill in the home district; he requested leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's mother fell ill in their home district; he asked leave to return.

sentences.zh: 值秋水暴長，河梁破絕，虬得一小船而渡，漏而不沒，時人異之。

translations.literal: When autumn waters rose suddenly and the river bridge was broken, Qiu obtained a small boat and crossed — leaking yet not sinking; men of the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn waters rose suddenly and the river bridge broke, Qiu obtained a small boat and crossed — leaking yet not sinking; men of the time marveled.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哀毀過禮，為時所稱。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he grieved beyond the rites — praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother, he grieved beyond the rites — praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 年四十九，卒。

translations.literal: Aged forty-nine, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of You province — posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of You province — posthumous epithet Wei.

sentences.zh: 虬善與人交，清河崔亮、頓丘李平並與親善。

translations.literal: Qiu was skilled at friendship; Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu were both close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was skilled at friendship; Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu were both on intimate terms with him.

sentences.zh: 所作碑頌雜筆三十餘篇。

translations.literal: He composed more than thirty stele inscriptions, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings.
translations.idiomatic: His stele inscriptions, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings numbered more than thirty.

sentences.zh: 有二子。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: There were two sons.

sentences.zh: 長子臧，在文苑傳。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zang — the account is in the Literary Garden biography.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Zang — the account appears in the Literary Garden biography.

sentences.zh: 臧弟子才，武定末，太常卿。

translations.literal: Zang's younger brother's son Cai, at the end of Wuding, was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Zang's nephew Cai, at the end of Wuding, served as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 虬從子策，亦有才學。

translations.literal: Qiu's nephew's son Ce also had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's nephew's son Ce likewise had talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 卒於齊王儀同開府主簿。

translations.literal: He died as Chief Clerk in the Prince of Qi's Staff of the Same Rank as the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Chief Clerk on the Prince of Qi's Staff of the Same Rank as the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 李平，字曇定，頓丘人也，彭城王嶷之長子。

translations.literal: Li Ping, courtesy name Tanding, was a native of Dunqiu — eldest son of Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping, styled Tanding, was a native of Dunqiu — eldest son of Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.

sentences.zh: 少有大度。

translations.literal: From youth he had great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Even from youth he showed great magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵羣書，好禮、易，頗有文才。

translations.literal: When grown he read widely among the books, loved the Rites and Changes, and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he read widely, loved the Rites and Changes, and had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜通直散騎侍郎，高祖禮之甚重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; Emperor Gaozu treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; Emperor Gaozu treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 頻經大憂，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: He repeatedly suffered great bereavement and was famed for filial mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered repeated bereavements and was famed for filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 後以例降，襲爵彭城公。

translations.literal: Later by precedent he was demoted in rank and inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent demoted in rank, he inherited the dukedom of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 拜太子中舍人，遷散騎侍郎，舍人如故，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was appointed Crown Prince's Household Attendant, promoted to Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining his household post, then promoted to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Crown Prince's Household Attendant, promoted to Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining his household post, then Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.

sentences.zh: 平因侍從容請自效一郡，高祖曰：「卿復欲以吏事自試也。」

translations.literal: Ping, while attending in easy conversation, requested to prove himself in one commandery; Emperor Gaozu said, "You again wish to test yourself in administrative affairs."
translations.idiomatic: While attending in relaxed conversation, Ping asked to prove himself in one commandery; Emperor Gaozu said, "You wish again to test yourself in administrative affairs."

sentences.zh: 拜長樂太守，政務清靜，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Changle; his governance was clear and quiet and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Changle; his rule was clear and quiet, and officials and people held him dear.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，以平兼冀州儀同開府長史，甚著聲稱，仍除正長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he was appointed Concurrent Chief Clerk of the Staff of the Same Rank as the Grand General's Office for Ji province, winning great renown, then appointed full Chief Clerk, retaining his administrator's post.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he was appointed Concurrent Chief Clerk of the Staff of the Same Rank as the Grand General's Office for Ji province, winning great renown, then full Chief Clerk, retaining his administrator's post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂行河南尹，豪右權貴憚之。

translations.literal: Before long he acted as Intendant of Henan; powerful gentry and noble families feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served as acting Intendant of Henan; powerful gentry and noble families feared him.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，除黃門郎，遷司徒左長史，行尹如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, acting as Intendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, continuing as acting Intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋以稱職正尹，長史如故。

translations.literal: Soon, for competence, he was made full Intendant, retaining his chief clerk's post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for distinguished service, he was confirmed as full Intendant while retaining his chief clerk's post.

sentences.zh: 車駕將幸鄴，平上表諫曰：「伏見己丑詔書，雲軒鑾輅，行幸有期，鳳服龍驂，剋駕近日。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was about to visit Ye; Ping submitted a memorial remonstrating: "I have seen the edict of the jichou day: the cloud-canopied carriage and imperial palanquin are to set out on a fixed date; phoenix-robed with dragon-harnessed steeds, the journey will depart within days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to visit Ye; Li Ping submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have read the edict of the jichou day, which announces that the imperial carriage will depart on a set date—that phoenix-robed escort and dragon-harnessed steeds will soon be on the road.

sentences.zh: 將欲講武淇陽，大習鄴魏，馳驌騻於綠竹之區，騁驎驥於漳滏之壤。

translations.literal: He intends to conduct military exercises at Qiyang and hold great maneuvers at Ye and Wei, to gallop piebald steeds through groves of green bamboo and to run thoroughbred chargers across the lands of the Zhang and Fu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He plans to review troops at Qiyang and stage grand exercises at Ye and Wei—to let piebald horses thunder through bamboo groves and let thoroughbreds race the banks of the Zhang and Fu.

sentences.zh: 斯誠幽顯同忻，人靈共悅。

translations.literal: This is indeed a matter in which the hidden and the manifest alike rejoice, and human and spirit worlds share delight.
translations.idiomatic: Truly this would bring joy to heaven and earth alike, and delight to gods and men together.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚管，竊有惑焉。

translations.literal: In my foolish narrow view, I privately have doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my humble judgment I cannot help but harbor doubts.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 嵩京創構，洛邑俶營，雖年跨十稔，根基未就。

translations.literal: Song's capital was newly founded and Luoyang newly begun; though more than ten years have passed, the foundations are not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: The new capital at Song was only just raised and Luoyang only just begun—though more than a decade has passed, the foundations are still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 代民至洛，始欲向盡，資產罄於遷移，牛畜斃於輦運，陵太行之險，越長津之難，辛勤備經，得達京闕，富者猶損太半，貧者可以意知。

translations.literal: When the people of Dai came to Luoyang, they at first meant to use up all they had; assets were exhausted by the move, cattle and livestock perished in cart transport; they endured the peril of Mount Taihang and the hardship of long fords—after every sort of toil they reached the capital gates, yet even the wealthy lost more than half, and the poor need hardly be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Dai arrived in Luoyang they poured out everything they owned: fortunes were drained by relocation, draft animals died on the road, and they braved Taihang's cliffs and long river crossings. After every hardship they reached the capital—yet even the rich lost more than half their wealth, and the poor fared far worse.

sentences.zh: 兼歷歲從戎，不遑啟處，自景明已來，差得休息。

translations.literal: Moreover they have for years followed the army and had no leisure to settle; since the Jingming era they have barely had rest.
translations.idiomatic: They have moreover campaigned year after year without respite; only since the Jingming reign have they begun to recover.

sentences.zh: 事農者未積二年之儲，築室者裁有數間之屋，莫不肆力伊瀍，人急其務。

translations.literal: Those who farm have not yet stored two years' grain; those who build houses have scarcely a few rooms—everyone is exerting strength along the Yi and Chan, and the people are urgent in their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers have not yet laid up two years' provisions; builders have only a few rooms to their name. All are straining along the Yi and Chan, every hand pressed to urgent work.

sentences.zh: 實宜安靜新人，勸其稼穡，令國有九年之糧，家有水旱之備。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to settle the newcomers in peace and encourage their farming, so that the state has nine years' grain and every household provision against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely the time to let the newcomers settle and encourage their planting, until the realm holds nine years' grain and every home keeps stores against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 若乘之以羈紲，則所廢多矣。

translations.literal: If they are driven with bridles and halters, much will be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If they are yoked to corvée and conscription, far more will be lost.

sentences.zh: 一夫從役，舉家失業。

translations.literal: When one man enters service, the whole household loses its livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: One man taken for service means an entire household left without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今復秋稼盈田，禾菽遍野，鑾駕所幸，騰踐必殷。

translations.literal: Now again the autumn crop fills the fields and millet and beans cover the countryside; wherever the imperial carriage passes, trampling will surely be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain now fills the fields and beans blanket the countryside; wherever the imperial procession treads, crops will be crushed underfoot.

sentences.zh: 未若端拱中天，坐招四海，耀武崧原，禮射伊洛，士馬無跋涉之勞，兆民有康哉之詠，可不美歟？」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to sit upright at the center and summon the four seas, to display martial prowess on Mount Song's plain and perform archery rites on the Yi and Luo—so that soldiers and horses know no wearisome marches and the myriad people sing of peace? Would this not be beautiful?"
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold court at the center and draw the four seas to you—to show martial splendor on Song's heights and perform the archery rites on the Yi and Luo, so that troops need no long march and the people may sing of peace. Would that not be the finer course?

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was rejected.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官行相州事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to act as regional inspector of Xiangzhou while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to govern Xiangzhou in his existing capacity.

sentences.zh: 世宗至鄴，親幸平第，見其諸子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong reached Ye he personally visited Ping's residence and met his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong arrived at Ye he visited Ping's home in person and saw his sons.

sentences.zh: 尋正刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made regular regional inspector and additionally appointed General Who Pacifies Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed as regional inspector and given the additional title General Who Pacifies Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 平勸課農桑，修飾太學，簡試通儒以充博士，選五郡聰敏者以教之，圖孔子及七十二子於堂，親為立讚。

translations.literal: Ping encouraged farming and sericulture, restored the Imperial Academy, selected broadly learned scholars to serve as erudites, chose clever youths from five commanderies to instruct, painted Confucius and the seventy-two disciples in the hall, and personally composed encomia for them.
translations.idiomatic: Ping promoted agriculture and sericulture, refurbished the Imperial Academy, tested broadly learned scholars for appointment as erudites, selected the brightest youths from five commanderies to teach, had portraits of Confucius and the seventy-two disciples painted in the hall, and wrote encomia for them himself.

sentences.zh: 前來臺使頗好侵取，平乃畫「履虎尾」、「踐薄冰」於客館，注頌其下，以示誡焉。

translations.literal: Former imperial envoys had been much given to extortion; Ping therefore painted "Treading a tiger's tail" and "Walking on thin ice" in the guest lodge and inscribed encomia beneath them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys had often abused their power to extort; Ping painted "Treading the tiger's tail" and "Walking on thin ice" in the guest lodge and added encomia below as a warning.

sentences.zh: 加平東將軍，徵拜長兼度支尚書，尋正尚書，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East, summoned and appointed concurrently as Director of the Department of Revenue, soon made regular Director of the Masters of Writing, and also served as Inspector of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, appointed concurrently Director of the Department of Revenue, soon made regular Director of the Masters of Writing, and given the concurrent post of Inspector of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史、京兆王愉反於信都，以平為使持節、都督北討諸軍事、鎮北將軍，行冀州事以討之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, regional inspector of Jizhou, rebelled at Xindu; Ping was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of the Northern Campaign, General Who Pacifies the North, and acting regional inspector of Jizhou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, regional inspector of Jizhou, rebelled at Xindu, Ping was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of the Northern Campaign, General Who Pacifies the North, and acting regional inspector of Jizhou to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨式乾殿，勞遣平曰：「愉，朕之元弟，居不疑之地，豺狼之心，不意而發，欲上傾社稷，下殘萬姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong came to the Shiqian Hall, saw Ping off with words of encouragement, and said: "Yu is my eldest brother by blood; he stood in a position beyond suspicion, yet the heart of a wolf and jackal erupted unlooked-for—he would overturn the altars of state above and slaughter the myriad people below.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came to the Shiqian Hall to send Ping off with encouragement: "Yu is my own elder brother, placed beyond all suspicion—yet the heart of a wolf flared up unlooked-for. He would topple the altars of state and slaughter the people.

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，夫豈獲止。

translations.literal: To destroy kin for righteousness—how could one stop short?
translations.idiomatic: To put righteousness above kinship—how could I hold back?

sentences.zh: 周公行之於古，朕亦當行之於今。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did this in antiquity; I too must do it today.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou did this in ancient times; I must do the same now.

sentences.zh: 委卿以專征之任，必令應期摧殄，務盡經略之規，勿虧推轂之寄也。

translations.literal: I entrust you with sole command; you must destroy the rebels within the appointed time, exhaust every plan of strategy, and not fail the trust placed in you as commander.
translations.idiomatic: I entrust you with full command. Crush them within the appointed time, leave no stratagem untried, and do not betray the trust invested in you.

sentences.zh: 何圖今日言及斯事。」

translations.literal: Who would have thought that today we should speak of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought the day would come when I must speak of this.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: He thereupon sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 平對曰：「臣愉天迷其心，構此梟悖。

translations.literal: Ping replied: "My lord Yu has been deluded in heart and contrived this rebellious treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Ping replied: "Prince Yu's heart has been clouded, and he has raised this treason.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不武，委以總督之任，今大宥既敷，便應有征無戰。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming me lacking in martial skill, has entrusted me with overall command; now that great clemency has been proclaimed, there should be campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, not judging me unfit for war, has given me overall command. Now that Your Majesty's clemency has been proclaimed, they should submit without a fight.

sentences.zh: 脫守迷不悟者，當仰憑天威，抑厲將士，譬猶太陽之消微露，巨海之蕩熒燭，天時人事，滅在昭然。

translations.literal: If any who hold to their delusion do not awaken, I shall rely on Heaven's majesty and restrain and rouse the officers and soldiers—just as the sun dispels a wisp of dew or the great sea washes away a flickering candle; in Heaven's season and human affairs, their destruction is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If any remain deluded and refuse to yield, I shall lean on Heaven's majesty and steel the troops—as the sun melts morning dew, as the ocean swallows a candle-flame. Heaven and earth have already decreed their ruin.

sentences.zh: 如其稽顙軍門，則送之大理，若不悛待戮，則鳴鼓釁鍾，非陛下之事。」

translations.literal: If he prostrates himself at the army gate, I shall send him to the Court of Justice; if he will not repent and awaits execution, then beat the drums and strike the bell of war—that is no longer Your Majesty's affair."
translations.idiomatic: If he kneels at the camp gate, I shall send him to the Court of Justice; if he will not repent and awaits the blade, then drums and war-gongs—that will no longer be Your Majesty's concern."

sentences.zh: 平進次經縣，諸軍大集。

translations.literal: Ping advanced and encamped at Jing County; the armies gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Ping moved forward and encamped at Jing County, where the armies massed.

sentences.zh: 夜有蠻兵數千斫平前壘，矢及平帳，平堅臥不動，俄而乃定。

translations.literal: By night several thousand barbarian soldiers hacked at Ping's forward ramparts; arrows reached Ping's tent, yet Ping lay firm and unmoving, and soon all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: By night several thousand tribal soldiers struck at Ping's forward ramparts; arrows pierced his tent, yet he lay still until the disturbance passed.

sentences.zh: 遂至冀州城南十六里。

translations.literal: He then reached a point sixteen li south of Jizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to sixteen li south of the Jizhou capital.

sentences.zh: 賊攻圍濟州軍，拔柵填塹，未滿者數尺。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged the Jizhou army, pulled up palisades and filled moats, leaving gaps of only a few feet unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged the Jizhou force, tearing up palisades and filling the moat until only a few feet remained open.

sentences.zh: 諸將合戰，無利而還，憚於更進。

translations.literal: The generals joined battle but gained no advantage and withdrew, fearing to advance again.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fought without gain and fell back, afraid to press forward again.

sentences.zh: 平親入行間，勸以重賞，士卒乃前，大破逆眾。

translations.literal: Ping personally entered the ranks and encouraged them with heavy rewards; the soldiers then pressed forward and utterly routed the rebel host.
translations.idiomatic: Ping walked among the ranks himself, promising rich rewards; the men surged forward and broke the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 愉時墜馬，乃有一人下馬授愉，止而鬬死。

translations.literal: Yu at that moment fell from his horse; one man dismounted and gave Yu his horse, halting to fight and die.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was thrown from his horse; a follower dismounted, gave Yu his mount, and died fighting where he stood.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，至於城門，斬首數萬級，遂圍城燒門。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit northward to the city gate, they beheaded tens of thousands, then besieged the city and burned the gate.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued north to the city gate, taking tens of thousands of heads, then invested the city and set the gate afire.

sentences.zh: 愉與百餘騎突門出走，遣統軍叔孫頭追之，去信都十里擒愉。

translations.literal: Yu broke out with a little over a hundred horsemen; Ping sent the commander Shusun Tou in pursuit and captured Yu ten li from Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fled with a little over a hundred riders; Ping sent Commander Shusun Tou after him and took Yu ten li from Xindu.

sentences.zh: 冀州平，世宗遣兼給事黃門侍郎、祕書丞元梵宣旨慰勞。

translations.literal: When Jizhou was pacified, Emperor Shizong sent the Concurrent Supervising Attendant Within the Yellow Gate and Secretary Director Yuan Fan to proclaim the imperial will and offer congratulations and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: After Jizhou was pacified, Shizong sent the concurrent Supervising Attendant Within the Yellow Gate and Secretary Director Yuan Fan with an imperial message of commendation.

sentences.zh: 徵還京師，以本官領相州大中正。

translations.literal: Summoned back to the capital, he retained his original office and additionally served as Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he kept his original post and was also made Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平先為尚書令高肇、侍御史王顯所恨，後顯代平為中尉，平加散騎常侍，顯劾平在冀州隱截官口，肇又扶成其狀，奏除平名。

translations.literal: Ping had earlier been hated by Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao and Attendant Imperial Secretary Wang Xian; afterward Xian replaced Ping as inspector, Ping was given the additional title Regular Attendant, and Xian impeached Ping for secretly seizing registered households in Jizhou—Zhao too supported the charge, and a memorial was submitted to remove Ping's name from office.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had long been hated by Director Gao Zhao and Attendant Imperial Secretary Wang Xian. When Xian replaced Ping as inspector, Ping was given the additional title Regular Attendant; Xian then impeached him for secretly seizing registered households in Jizhou, Zhao backed the accusation, and a memorial was submitted to strip him of rank.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，詔復官爵，除其定冀之勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanxing era an edict restored his office and title but removed credit for pacifying Ji and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanxing an edict restored his office and title but withheld credit for pacifying Ji and Ji.

sentences.zh: 前來良賤之訟，多有積年不決，平奏不問真偽，一以景明年前為限，於是諍訟止息。

translations.literal: Former lawsuits between free persons and bondsmen had often gone unresolved for years; Ping memorialized that, without asking whether claims were true or false, all should be limited to cases before the Jingming era, and litigation then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits between free and bonded persons had often dragged on for years. Ping proposed that, without inquiring into truth or falsehood, all cases be cut off at the Jingming era—and litigation ceased.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮民飢，鎮將任款請貸未許，擅開倉賑恤，有司繩以費散之條，免其官爵。

translations.literal: The people of Wuchuan garrison were starving; the garrison commander Ren Kuan requested grain on loan but was not permitted, yet he opened the granary on his own authority to relieve them; the authorities charged him under the statute on unauthorized disbursement and stripped him of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchuan garrison faced famine, Commander Ren Kuan asked for grain on loan and, denied permission, opened the granary on his own to feed the people. Officials charged him with unauthorized disbursement and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 平奏款意在濟人，心無不善，世宗原之。

translations.literal: Ping memorialized that Kuan's intent was to aid the people and his heart held no evil; Emperor Shizong pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping argued that Kuan's intent was to save lives and his heart was good; Shizong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; his post as Director of the Masters of Writing remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，轉吏部尚書，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong came to the throne he was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel and additionally General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 平高明強濟，所在有聲，但以性急為累。

translations.literal: Ping was lofty, bright, strong, and capable; wherever he served he won renown, yet he was hampered by a quick temper.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was brilliant, forceful, and effective; everywhere he served he made a name, though his quick temper was a handicap.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏理平定冀之勳，請酬以山河之賞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, Director of the Masters of Writing, memorialized to settle credit for Ping's pacification of Ji and requested reward with a fief in mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, petitioned to settle credit for Ping's pacification of Ji and asked that he be rewarded with a territorial fief.

sentences.zh: 靈太后乃封武邑郡開國公，食邑一千五百戶，縑二千五百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling thereupon enfeoffed him as Duke of Wuyi Commandery with a fief of fifteen hundred households and two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling then enfeoffed him Duke of Wuyi Commandery with fifteen hundred households and twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍遣其左游擊將軍趙祖悅偷據西硤石，眾至數萬，以逼壽春。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent his Left Mobile-Attack General Zhao Zuyue to seize Xixia Rock by stealth with a force numbering tens of thousands, pressing toward Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Yan had sent his Left Mobile-Attack General Zhao Zuyue to seize Xixia Rock by stealth with tens of thousands of men, threatening Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮南崔亮攻之，未克，又與李崇乖貳。

translations.literal: The Pacifier of the South Cui Liang attacked but could not take it, and moreover fell out with Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang, Pacifier of the South, besieged it without success and quarreled with Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 詔平以本官使持節、鎮軍大將軍、兼尚書右僕射為行臺，節度諸軍，東西州將一以禀之，如有乖異，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ping, in his original office, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, and Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing as mobile headquarters, directing all armies; generals of the eastern and western circuits were all to report to him, and any disobedience was to be punished by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was ordered, in his existing capacity, to serve as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, and Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing at mobile headquarters, commanding all forces. Eastern and western commanders were to obey him; disobedience would be punished by military law.

sentences.zh: 詔平長子奬以通直郎從，賜平縑帛百段、紫納金裝衫甲一領，賜奬縑布六十段、絳衲襖一領。

translations.literal: The edict also had Ping's eldest son Jiang accompany him as Attendant of Direct Communication and granted Ping one hundred sections of silk and brocade and one suit of purple-lined gold-trimmed armor; Jiang was granted sixty sections of silk and brocade and one purple-lined padded jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had Ping's eldest son Jiang accompany him as Attendant of Direct Communication. Ping received a hundred sections of silk and brocade and a suit of purple-lined gold-trimmed armor; Jiang received sixty sections and a purple-lined padded jacket.

sentences.zh: 父子重列，拜受家庭，觀者榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son both received honors together in the family courtyard; onlookers envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son received honors side by side at home, to the envy of all who saw.

sentences.zh: 於是率步騎二千以赴壽春。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led two thousand foot and horse to hurry to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then led two thousand infantry and cavalry to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 平巡視硤石內外，知其盈虛之所。

translations.literal: Ping inspected the inner and outer defenses of Xixia Rock and knew where strength and weakness lay.
translations.idiomatic: Ping surveyed Xixia Rock's inner and outer defenses and mapped its strengths and gaps.

sentences.zh: 嚴勒崇、亮，令水陸兼備，剋期齊舉。

translations.literal: He strictly ordered Chong and Liang to prepare both land and water forces and to strike together on the fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: He sternly ordered Chong and Liang to ready land and river forces alike and to attack together on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 崇、亮憚之，無敢乖互。

translations.literal: Chong and Liang feared him and dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Liang were afraid of him and did not dare act independently.

sentences.zh: 頻日交戰，屢破賊軍。

translations.literal: Day after day they joined battle and repeatedly defeated the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: Battle followed battle for days, and the enemy was beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍崔延伯立橋於下蔡，以拒賊之援軍。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the South Cui Yanbo built a bridge at Xia Cai to block the rebels' relief force.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the South Cui Yanbo built a bridge at Xia Cai to cut off enemy reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 賊將王神念、昌義之等不得進救，祖悅守死窮城。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not advance to rescue; Zuyue held the doomed city to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Wang Shennian and Chang Yizhi could not break through to help; Zuyue clung to the doomed fortress.

sentences.zh: 平乃部分攻之。

translations.literal: Ping then divided forces to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Ping then deployed his forces for the assault.

sentences.zh: 令崔亮督陸卒攻其城西，李崇勒水軍擊其東面，然後鼓噪，南北俱上。

translations.literal: He ordered Cui Liang to direct the land troops in attacking the west of the city and Li Chong to lead the river force against the east; then, at the drum's roar, both north and south mounted the walls together.
translations.idiomatic: He had Cui Liang lead the land force against the west wall and Li Chong the river force against the east; at the drum's signal both wings scaled the walls together.

sentences.zh: 賊眾周章，東西赴戰。

translations.literal: The rebel host was thrown into confusion, rushing east and west to the fight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel troops panicked, rushing back and forth to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 屠賊外城，賊之將士相率歸附。

translations.literal: They slaughtered their way into the outer city, and the rebel officers and soldiers surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the outer city, and rebel officers and soldiers surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 袓悅率其餘眾固保南城，通夜攻守，至明乃降。

translations.literal: Zuyue led his remaining force to hold the south city firm; they fought through the night until dawn, when they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyue held the south city with what remained of his force, fighting through the night until he surrendered at dawn.

sentences.zh: 斬袓悅，送首於洛，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Zuyue was beheaded and his head sent to Luoyang; captives were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyue was executed, his head sent to Luoyang, and captives were many.

sentences.zh: 以功遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional title Regular Attendant; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with the additional title Regular Attendant; his generalship was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 平還京師，靈太后見於宣光殿，賜以金裝刀杖一口。

translations.literal: When Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in the Xuan'guang Hall and granted him one gold-trimmed sword and staff.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, Ping was received by Empress Dowager Ling in the Xuan'guang Hall and given a gold-trimmed sword and staff.

sentences.zh: 時南徐州表云，蕭衍堰淮水為患，詔公卿議之，平以為不假兵力，終自毀壞。

translations.literal: At that time the Southern Xuzhou memorial reported that Xiao Yan was damming the Huai River to cause harm; an edict ordered the high ministers to discuss it, and Ping held that without needing troops it would in the end destroy itself.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou reported that Xiao Yan was damming the Huai to cause flooding. When ministers were ordered to discuss the matter, Ping argued that no troops were needed—the dam would collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 及淮堰破，靈太后大悅，引群臣入宴，敕平前鳴簫管，肅宗手賜縑布百段。

translations.literal: When the Huai dam broke, Empress Dowager Ling was greatly pleased; she led the ministers into banquet and ordered Ping forward to play pipes and flutes; Emperor Suzong personally bestowed a hundred sections of silk and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai dam broke, Empress Dowager Ling was delighted. She feasted the ministers, had Ping play pipes and flutes, and Suzong personally granted him a hundred sections of silk and brocade.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年冬卒，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xiping he died, leaving instructions for a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in winter of Xiping 1, instructing that he be buried simply.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、帛七百匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted eastern-garden secret vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, and seven hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted eastern-garden funeral vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, and seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 靈太后為舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held mourning rites for him in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling mourned him in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡文烈公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Three Excellencies of Honor, and regional inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Three Excellencies of Honor, and regional inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Duke Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 平自在度支，至於端副，夙夜在公，孜孜匪懈，凡處機密十有餘年，有獻替之稱。

translations.literal: From the time Ping was in the Department of Revenue until he stood at the head of the secretariat, he toiled day and night in public service, diligent and untiring; in all he handled confidential affairs for more than ten years and won praise for offering counsel and making corrections.
translations.idiomatic: From his time in the Department of Revenue to his place at the head of the secretariat, Ping toiled day and night without slackening. For more than ten years he handled state secrets and won praise for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 所製詩賦箴諫詠頌，別有集錄。

translations.literal: The poems, fu, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and encomia he composed [13] were separately collected in a compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The poems, fu, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and encomia he wrote [13] were collected in a separate compilation.

sentences.zh: 平長子奬，字遵穆，襲。

translations.literal: Ping's eldest son Jiang, courtesy name Zunmu, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's eldest son Jiang, courtesy name Zunmu, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，有當世才度。

translations.literal: In appearance he was tall and imposing and possessed talent and bearing fit for the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, with talent and presence suited to his times.

sentences.zh: 自太尉參軍事，稍遷通直郎、中書侍郎、直閤將軍、吏部郎中、征虜將軍，遷安東將軍、光祿大夫，仍吏部郎中。

translations.literal: From aide in the Ministry of War he was gradually promoted to Attendant of Direct Communication, Gentleman of the Secretariat, General of the Direct Office, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and General Who Subdues Barbarians, then to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, still serving as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an aide in the Ministry of War, he rose through Attendant of Direct Communication, Gentleman of the Secretariat, General of the Direct Office, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and General Who Subdues Barbarians to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, still serving as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又以本官兼尚書，出為撫軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He also served in his original office concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing and went out as General Who Pacifies the Army and regional inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing and was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Army and regional inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元叉擅朝，奬為其親待，頻居顯要。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Cha monopolized the court, Jiang was treated as a kinsman and repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha dominated the court, Jiang was treated as kin and repeatedly held high office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，削除官爵。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule she stripped him of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she removed his rank and office.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，為散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaozhuang's reign he became Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 奬前後所歷，皆以明濟著稱。

translations.literal: In every post Jiang held before and after, he was noted for clarity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held, Jiang was known for clarity and competence.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，顥以奬兼尚書右僕射，慰勞徐州羽林及城人，不承顥旨，害奬，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hao made Jiang Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to comfort the Xuzhou guard cavalry and city people; they did not accept Hao's command and killed Jiang, sending his head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he made Jiang Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to reassure the Xuzhou guard and townspeople. They refused Hao's orders, killed Jiang, and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，奬故吏通直散騎常侍宋遊道上書理奬曰：「臣聞賞善罰惡，謂之二機，有道存焉，所貴不濫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu, Jiang's former subordinate Attendant of Direct Communication and Regular Attendant Song Youdao submitted a memorial on Jiang's behalf, saying: "I have heard that rewarding good and punishing evil are called the two mechanisms; where the Way exists, what is valued is not excess.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao petitioned on his behalf: "I have heard that rewarding virtue and punishing vice are the two hinges of governance; where the Way holds sway, what matters is that neither be applied too freely.

sentences.zh: 是以子胥無罪，吳人痛之；

translations.literal: Thus though Wu Zixu was guiltless, the people of Wu grieved for him;
translations.idiomatic: Thus though Wu Zixu was innocent, the people of Wu mourned him;

sentences.zh: 郤宛不幸，國言未息。

translations.literal: though Xi Wan met misfortune, the realm's talk did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: though Xi Wan met with misfortune, public outrage did not subside.

sentences.zh: 故河南尹李奬，門居戚里，世擅名家，有此良才，是兼周用。

translations.literal: The former Intendant of Henan Li Jiang came from an imperial affinal house and for generations dominated a famous clan; possessing such fine talent, he was fit for broad employment.
translations.idiomatic: The former Intendant of Henan, Li Jiang, came from an imperial affinal house and a distinguished clan; gifted as he was, he was fit for the highest service.

sentences.zh: 自少及長，忠孝為心，入朝出牧，清明流譽。

translations.literal: From youth to maturity loyalty and filial piety were his heart; entering court or going out to govern, clarity flowed in his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to manhood loyalty and filial piety shaped his heart; in court or in the provinces his name stood for integrity.

sentences.zh: 襟懷放暢，風神爽發，實廊廟之瑚璉，社稷之楨幹。

translations.literal: Broad-minded and free in spirit, bright and quick in bearing, he was truly a ritual vessel of the hall of state and a pillar of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Open in spirit and quick in bearing, he was truly a ritual vessel of the state and a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 往歲，北海竊據，負扆當朝，王公卿士，俛眉從事。

translations.literal: In past years, when the Prince of Beihai seized power and sat facing the screen to hold court, princes, dukes, and ministers bowed their brows and followed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when the Prince of Beihai seized power and held court, princes, dukes, and ministers bowed and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 而奬闔門百口，同居京洛，既被覊縶，自拔無由。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang's household of a hundred mouths lived together in Luoyang; once bound in captivity, there was no way to free himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiang's household of a hundred mouths lived together in Luoyang; once bound, he had no means of escape.

sentences.zh: 託使東南，情存避難，當時物論謂其得所。

translations.literal: Entrusting himself to a mission to the southeast, his feeling was to avoid disaster; opinion at the time said he had found his place.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on a mission to the southeast, he sought only to survive; public opinion at the time held that he had chosen wisely.

sentences.zh: 然北海未敗之日，徐州刺史元孚為其純臣，莫之敢距，表啟相望，遲速唯命。

translations.literal: Yet before Beihai's defeat, the regional inspector of Xuzhou Yuan Fu was his loyal minister and none dared resist; memorials and reports followed one after another, and pace obeyed only his command.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before Beihai fell, Xuzhou's regional inspector Yuan Fu was his loyal follower and none dared resist; memorials streamed in and all awaited his word.

sentences.zh: 及皇輿返正，神器斯復，輕薄之徒，共生僥倖，詭言要賞，曲道求通，濫及善人，稱為己力。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to right rule and the sacred vessel was restored, frivolous men bred fresh hopes; with deceitful words they sought reward, by crooked paths they sought advancement, and they recklessly dragged good men into claims of their own merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was restored and the sacred vessel recovered, the frivolous seized their chance—spinning false tales for reward, bending rules for advancement, and claiming credit for good men's deeds.

sentences.zh: 若以奬受命賊朝，語跡成罪，便與天下共當此責。

translations.literal: If receiving orders from the rebel court makes Jiang guilty by word and deed, then the whole realm must share this blame together.
translations.idiomatic: If taking orders from the rebel court makes Jiang guilty by word and deed, then the whole court must share that guilt.

sentences.zh: 于時朝旨唯命免官，亦既經恩，方加酷濫。

translations.literal: At that time the court's intent was only to remove him from office; he had already received grace, yet cruel excess was added afterward.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court meant only to dismiss him from office; he had already been shown mercy, yet afterward cruel excess was piled on.

sentences.zh: 伊昔具臣，比肩賊所，身臨河上，日尋干戈，時逢寬政，任遇不改。
