translations.literal: In former days worthy ministers stood shoulder to shoulder in the rebel camp, themselves on the riverbank seeking battle day after day; they met a lenient policy and their appointments did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In former days worthy ministers stood side by side in the rebel camp, themselves on the riverbank fighting day after day—yet under a lenient policy their posts went unchanged.

sentences.zh: 一介使人，獨嬰斯戮，凡在有心，孰不嗟悼！

translations.literal: Yet one lone envoy alone suffered this slaughter; all who have a heart—who does not sigh and mourn!
translations.idiomatic: Yet one lone envoy alone suffered this slaughter—who with a heart does not mourn?

sentences.zh: 前朝所以論功者，見其邊人且相慰悅，其猶郭默生亂，劉胤懸首，事乃權宜，蓋非實錄。

translations.literal: The reason the former court counted his merit was that it saw the border people somewhat comforted and pleased; like Guo Mo's rebellion and Liu Yin's head hung up, the affair was expedient and not a true record.
translations.idiomatic: The former court counted his merit only because border people seemed reassured—as with Guo Mo's revolt and Liu Yin's head on display, the affair was expedient, not a true reckoning.

sentences.zh: 昔鄧艾下世，段灼理其冤；

translations.literal: In former times when Deng Ai died, Duan Zhuo addressed his injustice;
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai died, Duan Zhuo pleaded his injustice;

sentences.zh: 馬援物故，朱勃申其屈。

translations.literal: when Ma Yuan passed away, Zhu Bo declared his wrong.
translations.idiomatic: when Ma Yuan died, Zhu Bo pleaded his case.

sentences.zh: 臣雖小人，趣事君子，有懷舊恩，義兼人故，見其若此，久欲陳辭。

translations.literal: Though I am a petty man, I attend upon gentlemen; cherishing old kindness, my righteousness joins with human ties—seeing him treated thus, I have long wished to speak.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a petty man who serves gentlemen; remembering old kindness and bound by human ties, seeing him treated thus I have long wished to speak.

sentences.zh: 含言未吐，遂至今日，幽泉已閉，壟樹成行，內手捫心，顧懷愧慨。

translations.literal: Words held back and not spoken reached today; the dark spring is already closed and tomb trees stand in rows—pressing hand to heart within, I look back with shame and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Words I held back have reached this day; the grave is closed and tomb trees stand in rows—I press my hand to my heart in shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 幸逢興聖，理運唯新，雖曰纂戎，事同創革。

translations.literal: Fortunately we meet a sage arising and reason's fortune renewed; though it is called succeeding to arms, the affair is like founding anew.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately we meet a sage on the throne and an age renewed; though called succession, it is like a new founding.

sentences.zh: 頻有大恩，被於率土，亡官失爵者悉蒙追復。

translations.literal: Again and again great grace has covered the realm; those who lost office and title have all received restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Great grace has repeatedly covered the realm; those stripped of rank have all been restored.

sentences.zh: 而奬雜木猶存，牛車未改。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang, like a stray tree still standing, remains an ox-cart unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiang, like a stray tree still standing, remains unredeemed.

sentences.zh: 士感知己，懷此無忘，輕率瞽言，干犯輦轂。

translations.literal: Scholars who know a true friend hold this and do not forget; with light rash blind words I offend the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Those who know loyalty hold this and do not forget; with rash words I offend the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，賜垂矜覽，加其贈秩，慰此幽魂。」

translations.literal: I bow and hope Heaven's mirror may bestow compassionate reading, add posthumous rank, and comfort this shade in the dark."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Heaven's mirror to look with compassion, grant posthumous rank, and comfort his shade.

sentences.zh: 詔贈衞將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Guard General and regional inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Guard General and regional inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子構，襲。

translations.literal: His son Gou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gou succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was Attendant in the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he served as Attendant in the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 構弟訓，太尉默曹參軍。

translations.literal: Gou's younger brother Xun was an aide in the Ministry of War's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's younger brother Xun served as an aide in the Ministry of War's Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奬弟諧，字虔和。

translations.literal: Jiang's younger brother Xie, courtesy name Qianhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's younger brother was Xie, styled Qianhe.

sentences.zh: 風流閑潤，博學有文辯，當時才俊，咸相欽賞。

translations.literal: Refined and easy in manner, broadly learned with literary eloquence, he was admired and honored by the talented men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and polished, broadly learned and eloquent, he was admired by the leading men of his day.

sentences.zh: 受父前爵彭城侯。

translations.literal: He received his father's former title Marquis of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's former title, Marquis of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 自太尉參軍，歷尚書郎、徐州北海王顥撫軍府司馬，入為長兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: From aide in the Ministry of War he passed through Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and staff officer in the Pacification Headquarters of the Prince of Beihai of Xuzhou, Yuan Hao, entering the capital as Concurrent Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From aide in the Ministry of War he served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and staff officer to Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of Xuzhou, then entered the capital as Concurrent Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 崔光引為兼著作郎，諧在史職，無所歷意。

translations.literal: Cui Guang brought him in as Concurrent Compiler in the History Office; Xie, in the historiographical post, applied no effort of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang appointed him Concurrent Compiler in the History Office; Xie, in that post, applied no real effort.

sentences.zh: 加輔國將軍、相州大中正、光祿大夫，除金紫光祿大夫，加衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles General Who Assists the State, Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; removed as Grand Master of Golden Splendor and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and given the additional title Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made additionally General Who Assists the State, Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then Grand Master of Golden Splendor and additionally Guard General.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he was made Supervising Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Xie was appointed Supervising Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，除名，乃為述身賦曰：

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated his name was removed from the rolls, and he thereupon composed the "Fu on Describing the Self":
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of rank after Hao's defeat, he composed the "Fu on Describing the Self":

sentences.zh: 夫休咎相躡，禍福相生。

translations.literal: Fortune and calamity tread on each other's heels; disaster and blessing beget one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and calamity walk in each other's footsteps; disaster and blessing give birth to one another.

sentences.zh: 龜筮迷其兆，聖達蔽其萌。

translations.literal: Tortoise and milfoil divination confuse their omens; sages and the enlightened veil their first sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoise shells and milfoil stalks blur their signs; even sages cannot see calamity at its first sprouting.

sentences.zh: 覽成敗於前迹，料趣捨於人情。

translations.literal: Surveying success and failure in former tracks, I measure advance and retreat by human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Reading success and failure in the traces of the past, I weigh advance and retreat by the measure of human hearts.

sentences.zh: 咸爭途以走利，罕外己以逃名。

translations.literal: All contend on the road to seize profit; few look outside themselves to flee fame.
translations.idiomatic: All race the road to profit; few step outside themselves to escape renown.

sentences.zh: 連從車以載禍，多廐馬以取刑。

translations.literal: Linking follow-carts to carry disaster, keeping many stable horses to invite punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They hitch their carts to power and invite ruin; they keep many horses in the stable and court punishment.

sentences.zh: 豈知夫一介獨往，乃千乘所不能傾。

translations.literal: How could they know that one man going alone cannot be overturned even by a thousand chariots?
translations.idiomatic: Little do they know that one man walking alone cannot be toppled even by a thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 伊薄躬之悔吝，無性命之淑靈。

translations.literal: Alas for my slight person and its regrets—no fair spirit of life.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my humble self and its regrets—I was granted no fair portion of life's grace.

sentences.zh: 藉休庸於祖武，仰餘烈於家聲。

translations.literal: I borrowed my ancestors' martial merit and looked up to the lingering glory of the family name.
translations.idiomatic: I leaned on my forebears' martial merit and looked up to the lingering glory of our house.

sentences.zh: 徒從師以下學，乏遊道於上京。

translations.literal: I merely followed teachers to study below; I lacked roaming the Way in the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: I merely followed teachers in lower learning; I never wandered the Way in the great capital.

sentences.zh: 洎方年之四五，實始筮之弱齡。

translations.literal: When I reached four or five years of age, it was truly the weak years of first divination.
translations.idiomatic: When I reached four or five, I was still in the tender years of first divination.

sentences.zh: 爰釋巾而從吏，謬邀寵於時明。

translations.literal: Then I put aside the towel and followed the clerks, wrongly seeking favor in a bright age.
translations.idiomatic: Then I put aside the scholar's cloth and entered office, wrongly seeking favor in a bright age.

sentences.zh: 彼□□之赫赫，乃陋周而小漢。

translations.literal: That [lacuna] in its blaze and splendor—yet it made Zhou seem small and Han seem petty.
translations.idiomatic: That [lacuna] in its blaze and splendor—it made Zhou seem narrow and Han seem small.

sentences.zh: 帝文篤其成功，我武治其未亂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was earnest in his completed achievement; our martial house governed before disorder came.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was earnest in completing the work; our martial house governed before chaos could arise.

sentences.zh: 掩四奧而同軌，穆三辰而貞觀。

translations.literal: It covered the four corners and made one track; it harmonized the three luminaries and held correct observation.
translations.idiomatic: It covered the four quarters and made one road; it harmonized sun, moon, and stars in a reign of right rule.

sentences.zh: 威北暢而武戢，鼎南遷而文煥。

translations.literal: Its might flowed north while arms were stilled; the cauldron moved south while culture blazed anew.
translations.idiomatic: Its might spread north while arms were sheathed; the cauldron moved south while culture flamed anew.

sentences.zh: 異人相趨於絳闕，鴻生接武於儒館。

translations.literal: Strange men hastened together at the crimson gate; great scholars linked steps at the Confucian halls.
translations.idiomatic: Strange talents flocked to the crimson gate; great scholars walked in succession at the halls of learning.

sentences.zh: 總羣雅而同歸，果方員而殊貫。

translations.literal: Gathering all elegance they returned as one; square and round in talent yet each with a different thread.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering all refinement they converged as one—square and round in talent, each with a different thread.

sentences.zh: 伊濫吹之所從，初竊服於宰旅。

translations.literal: Ah, from the place of indiscriminate piping I first stole rank among the host of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Ah—from the ranks of indiscriminate piping I first stole a place among the clerks.

sentences.zh: 奉盛王之高義，遊兔園而容與。

translations.literal: Serving the great king's lofty righteousness, I wandered the Rabbit Garden at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the great king's lofty righteousness, I wandered at ease in the Rabbit Garden.

sentences.zh: 綴鴻鷺之末行，連英髦之茂序。

translations.literal: I joined the last ranks of swans and egrets and linked the flourishing order of outstanding youths.
translations.idiomatic: I joined the last ranks of swans and egrets and kept company with the finest youths of the age.

sentences.zh: 及伯舅之西伐，赫靈旗之東舉。

translations.literal: When the elder uncle by marriage marched west, the spirit banner blazed eastward.
translations.idiomatic: When my uncle by marriage marched west, the imperial banner blazed eastward.

sentences.zh: 復奉役於前轅，仍執覊於後距。

translations.literal: Again I served in the front axle-shaft and still was held in bonds at the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Again I served at the front axle and still was held in bonds at the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 迫玄冬之暮歲，歷關山之遐阻。

translations.literal: Forced in the deep winter of the year's end, I crossed the long passes of distant barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Forced in deep winter at year's end, I crossed long passes and distant barriers.

sentences.zh: 風激沙而破石，雪浮河而漫野。

translations.literal: Wind whipped sand and broke stone; snow floated on the river and flooded the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Wind whipped sand against stone; snow drifted on the river and drowned the plain.

sentences.zh: 樂在志其無端，悲涉物而多緒。

translations.literal: Joy lay in the will without cause; grief crossed things and bore many threads of feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Joy lay in a will without root; grief touched every thing and bore many threads of feeling.

sentences.zh: 俄宮車之晏駕，改乘轅而歸予。

translations.literal: Soon the palace carriage halted in its journey; the axle-shaft was changed and I was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the imperial carriage halted on its journey; the axle was changed and I was sent home.

sentences.zh: 屬推恩之在今，自傍枝而禔福。

translations.literal: Just then grace extended in the present; from a collateral branch I received blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Grace fell in my own day; from a collateral line I drew my share of fortune.

sentences.zh: 既獻□以命宗，叨微躬於侯服。

translations.literal: Having presented [lacuna] to command the clan, I wrongly received my slight person in a marquis's fief.
translations.idiomatic: Having presented [lacuna] to head the clan, I unworthily took a marquis's fief upon my humble self.

sentences.zh: 禮空文於覜饗，賦無征於湯沐。

translations.literal: Rites were empty words at the audience feast; tribute had no levy for bathing and washing.
translations.idiomatic: Court rites were hollow at the audience feast; no tribute was levied for the lord's bath.

sentences.zh: 思守位而匪懈，每屏居而自肅。

translations.literal: I thought to keep my place without slackness and often withdrew to my quarters to discipline myself.
translations.idiomatic: I resolved to hold my post without slack and often withdrew to my rooms to keep myself in check.

sentences.zh: 忽忝命於建禮，遊丹綺之重複。

translations.literal: Suddenly I was honored with appointment at Jianli and wandered the layered crimson silks.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly I was honored with office at Jianli and walked among layered halls of crimson silk.

sentences.zh: 信茲選之為難，乃上應於列宿。

translations.literal: Truly this selection was difficult; it answered above to the ranks of stars.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the choice was hard—it matched, above, the ordering of the stars.

sentences.zh: 陽源猶且自免，何稱仲治與太叔。

translations.literal: If Yang Yuan could still excuse himself, how could one name Zhongzhi and Taishu?
translations.idiomatic: If even Yang Yuan could beg off, what of men like Zhongzhi and Taishu?

sentences.zh: 余生□之蕭散，本寓名而為仕。

translations.literal: My remaining life [lacuna] in its free scatter—I originally lodged my name in office only as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of my days [lacuna], scattered and free—I took office only as a lodging for my name.

sentences.zh: 好不存於吏法，才實疏於政理。

translations.literal: What I liked was not stored in clerical law; talent was truly sparse in governance.
translations.idiomatic: What I loved lay outside clerical law; my talent was truly thin for governing.

sentences.zh: 竟火燭之不事，徒博弈其賢已。

translations.literal: At last I did not attend to fire and candle; I merely gambled at chess like the worthy already gone.
translations.idiomatic: At last I left fire and candle untended and merely played chess, like the sages before me.

sentences.zh: 竊自託於諸生，頗馳騁於文史。

translations.literal: Privately I entrusted myself to the scholars and somewhat ranged through literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: In private I cast my lot with scholars and ranged a little through literature and history.

sentences.zh: 通人假其餘論，士林察於□理。

translations.literal: Men of broad learning lent me their spare discourse; the forest of scholars observed my [lacuna] reason.
translations.idiomatic: Learned men lent me their spare talk; the grove of scholars weighed my [lacuna] mind.

sentences.zh: 乃妄涉於風流，遂飾輩於士子。

translations.literal: Then I rashly entered the currents of elegance and thus adorned myself among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Then I rashly entered elegant company and so dressed myself among gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 且以自託，□□□□。

translations.literal: And with this I entrusted myself [lacuna][lacuna][lacuna][lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: And so I made my refuge [lacuna][lacuna][lacuna][lacuna].

sentences.zh: 雖邇傒塵滓，而賞許雲霞。

translations.literal: Though close at hand one scorned the mire, yet one praised as cloud and rosy light.
translations.idiomatic: Though near at hand they scorned the mud, from afar they praised me as cloud and dawn-light.

sentences.zh: 栖閑虛以築館，背城闕而為家。

translations.literal: Dwelling in quiet emptiness I built a lodge, turning my back on the city gate to make a home.
translations.idiomatic: In quiet emptiness I built a lodge, turning my back on the city gate to make a home.

sentences.zh: 帶二學之高宇，遠三市之狹邪。

translations.literal: Bordered by the high halls of the two academies, far from the narrow lanes of the three markets.
translations.idiomatic: It lay beside the high halls of the two academies, far from the narrow lanes of the three markets.

sentences.zh: 事雖儉而未陋，製有度而不奢。

translations.literal: Affairs though frugal were not crude; construction had measure and was not extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Though frugal, nothing was crude; though measured, nothing was mean.

sentences.zh: 山隱勢於複石，水回流於激沙。

translations.literal: Mountains hid their force in layered stone; water turned back in rushing sand.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains banked their strength in stacked stone; water doubled back through rushing sand.

sentences.zh: 樹先春而動色，草迎歲而發花。

translations.literal: Trees moved color before spring; grass welcomed the year and sent forth flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Trees flushed with color before spring; grass greeted the year and broke into flower.

sentences.zh: 座有清談之客，門交好事之車。

translations.literal: Seats held guests of pure discourse; the gate received carriages of men who loved affairs.
translations.idiomatic: My seats held guests of pure talk; my gate received the carriages of men who loved good company.

sentences.zh: 或林嬉於月夜，或水宴於景斜。

translations.literal: Some frolicked in groves under the moon; some feasted on water as the light slanted.
translations.idiomatic: Some sported in groves beneath the moon; some feasted on the water as the light slanted.

sentences.zh: 肆雕章之腴旨，咀文藝之英華。

translations.literal: They unfolded the rich flavor of carved chapters and chewed the splendor of literary craft.
translations.idiomatic: We unfolded the rich savor of polished prose and tasted the splendor of literary craft.

sentences.zh: 羞綠芰與丹藕，薦朱李及甘瓜。

translations.literal: They set out green lotus and red lotus-root; they offered red plums and sweet melons.
translations.idiomatic: We served green lotus and red lotus-root, red plums and sweet melons.

sentences.zh: 雖慚洛水之名致，有類金谷之諠譁。

translations.literal: Though ashamed before the fame of the Luo waters, it was like the clamor of the Golden Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Though shamed before the fame of the Luo waters, our revel had something of the Golden Valley's clamor.

sentences.zh: 聊自足於所好，豈留連於或號。

translations.literal: I merely sufficed for what I loved—how could I linger on any title?
translations.idiomatic: I was content with what I loved—why linger over any title?

sentences.zh: 思炯戒而自反，勗身名於所蹈。

translations.literal: I thought bright warning and turned back upon myself, encouraging body and name in what I tread.
translations.idiomatic: I took bright warning to heart and turned inward, urging body and name along the path I walked.

sentences.zh: 奉哲后之淵猷，讚崇麾於華奧。

translations.literal: Serving the wise ruler's deep design, I praised the lofty banner in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the wise ruler's deep design, I sang the praises of his lofty banner.

sentences.zh: 豈千乘之乏使，感一眄之相勞。

translations.literal: Could a realm of a thousand chariots lack envoys? I was moved by a single glance of labor.
translations.idiomatic: Could a realm of a thousand chariots lack envoys? A single glance of favor moved me to serve.

sentences.zh: 竟不留於三月，因病滿而休告。

translations.literal: At last I was not kept for three months; because illness was full I requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: At last I was not kept three months; when illness had run its course I asked leave.

sentences.zh: 彼東觀之清華，乃任隆於載筆。

translations.literal: That Eastern Pavilion in its pure splendor—its charge was weighty in bearing the brush.
translations.idiomatic: That Eastern Pavilion, pure and splendid—its charge was weighty for the hand that bears the brush.

sentences.zh: 蔡一去而貽恨，張再還而有述。

translations.literal: When Cai went once he left regret; when Zhang returned twice he had something to tell.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, going once, left regret behind; Zhang, returning twice, had a tale to tell.

sentences.zh: 忽牽短而濫官，司惇史於藏室。

translations.literal: Suddenly, dragged short into an unworthy office, I was charged with honest history in the archive chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly, unfit and overmatched, I was thrust into office and charged with honest history in the archive chamber.

sentences.zh: 慚班子之繁麗，微馬生之簡實。

translations.literal: Ashamed before Ban's son in his luxuriant style, I was slight before Master Ma in his plain truth.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed before Ban's son in his luxuriant style, I shrank before Master Ma in his plain truth.

sentences.zh: 復通籍而延寵，陪帝扃之華密。

translations.literal: Again I passed the gate and received extended favor, accompanying the emperor's door in its flowery secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Again I passed the palace gate and received extended favor, attending the emperor's door in flowery secrecy.

sentences.zh: 信儀鳳之所栖，乃絲文之自出。

translations.literal: Truly where the ceremonial phoenix rests—there silk and writing issue of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Truly where the ceremonial phoenix rests, silk and writing issue of themselves.

sentences.zh: 歷五載而徘徊，猶官命之不改。

translations.literal: For five years I lingered; still the command of office did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Five years I lingered, and still the command of office did not change.

sentences.zh: 謝能飛於無翼，故同滯於有待。

translations.literal: I thanked the one who could fly without wings; thus I was equally stalled in waiting.
translations.idiomatic: I thanked the one who could fly without wings—and so I too was stalled in waiting.

sentences.zh: 晚加秩於戎章，乃□號之斯在。

translations.literal: Late I was given rank in the military chapter—then [lacuna] title was there.
translations.idiomatic: Late came rank in the military chapter—then [lacuna] title was mine.

sentences.zh: 屬運道之將季，諒冠屨之無礙。

translations.literal: Just as the fortune of the Way was about to decline, I trusted that cap and shoes would not hinder.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the Way's fortune was about to fail, I trusted that cap and shoes would not hinder me.

sentences.zh: 奄昇御於鼎湖，忽流哀於四海。

translations.literal: Suddenly the emperor ascended at Dinghu; suddenly grief flowed through the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the emperor ascended at Dinghu; suddenly grief poured through the four seas.

sentences.zh: 昔漢命之中微，皇統於是三絕。

translations.literal: In former times when Han's mandate waned, the imperial line thrice was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when Han's mandate waned, the imperial line was cut off thrice.

sentences.zh: 暨孝昌之陵陂，亦繼□而禍結。

translations.literal: At the mound-slope of Xiaochang too, calamity knotted in succession [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaochang's mound-slope too, calamity knotted one upon another [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 將小雅之詩廢，復三綱之道滅。

translations.literal: The ode of the Lesser Elegantia would be abandoned; again the Way of the Three Bonds was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Elegantia would fall silent; again the Way of the Three Bonds was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 思跼蹐於時昏，獨沉吟於運閉。

translations.literal: I thought of cramping steps in the age's darkness and alone brooded in the closed fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I thought of cramped steps in a dark age and brooded alone while fortune closed in.

sentences.zh: 遂退處於窮里，不外交於人世。

translations.literal: Then I withdrew to a poor hamlet and did not outwardly mingle with the human world.
translations.idiomatic: Then I withdrew to a poor hamlet and kept no outward commerce with the world of men.

sentences.zh: 及數反於中興，驅時雄而電逝。

translations.literal: When restoration came again and again, the heroes of the age were driven like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: When restoration came again and again, the age's heroes were driven like lightning.

sentences.zh: 既籍取亂之權，方乘轉圓之勢。

translations.literal: Having borrowed the power to seize disorder, they then rode the momentum of turning the circle.
translations.idiomatic: Having borrowed the power to seize disorder, they rode the turning momentum of the wheel.

sentences.zh: 俄隙開而守廢，遂冠冕之毀裂。

translations.literal: Soon gaps opened and defense was abandoned; then caps and crowns were torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: Soon gaps opened, defense collapsed, and caps and crowns were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 彼膏原而塗野，嗟衞肝與嵇血。

translations.literal: There the fat plain was smeared over the wild; alas for Wei's liver and Ji's blood.
translations.idiomatic: There the fat plain was smeared across the wild—alas for Wei's liver and Ji's blood!

sentences.zh: 何古今之一揆，每治少而亂多。

translations.literal: Why ancient and modern follow one measure—each age has little order and much disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Why do ancient and modern follow one measure—in every age order is brief and disorder long?

sentences.zh: 盧遁身於東掖，荀窘迹於南羅。

translations.literal: Lu hid his body in the eastern side-room; Xun cramped his tracks in the southern net.
translations.idiomatic: Lu hid himself in the eastern side-room; Xun cramped his tracks in the southern net.

sentences.zh: 時獲逃於□阜，仍竄宿於巖阿。

translations.literal: At times I escaped to [lacuna] mounds and still hid and lodged in cliff caves.
translations.idiomatic: At times I fled to [lacuna] mounds and still hid and lodged in cliff caves.

sentences.zh: 首丘急於明發，東路長其如何。

translations.literal: The mound-head was urgent at dawn's light; the eastern road was long—how could it be?
translations.idiomatic: Homeward longing pressed at dawn; the eastern road was long—what could I do?

sentences.zh: 遽登舟而鼓柂，乃沿洛而汎河。

translations.literal: Hurriedly I boarded the boat and beat the oar, then followed the Luo and floated the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hurriedly I boarded, beat the oar, and followed the Luo out onto the river.

sentences.zh: 騖寸陰於不測，競征鳥於歸波。

translations.literal: I raced an inch of shade into the unknowable and vied with the homeward bird on the returning wave.
translations.idiomatic: I raced each inch of shade into the unknown and vied with homeward birds on the returning wave.

sentences.zh: 時在所而放命，連百萬於山東。

translations.literal: At the time they acted lawlessly wherever they were and linked a million men in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they acted lawlessly wherever they stood and linked a million men in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 何信都之巨猾，若封豕與大風。

translations.literal: What great villainy of Xindu—like a penned boar and a great wind.
translations.idiomatic: What villainy at Xindu—like a penned boar, like a great wind!

sentences.zh: 肆吞噬於觜距，咸邑燼而野空。

translations.literal: They devoured at beak and claw; cities burned and the wild was empty.
translations.idiomatic: They devoured with beak and claw; cities burned and the wild lay empty.

sentences.zh: 徑黎陽之寇聚，迫崖壘之渢隆。

translations.literal: Passing the bandits' gathering at Liyang, pressing the cliff ramparts' swelling danger.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the bandits' nest at Liyang, pressing cliff ramparts that swelled with danger.

sentences.zh: 躁通川而鼎沸，矢交射於舟中。

translations.literal: Restless, the open river seethed like a cauldron; arrows crossed and shot into the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Restless, the open river seethed like a cauldron; arrows crossed and struck the boat.

sentences.zh: 備百罹於茲日，諒陳蔡之非窮。

translations.literal: A hundred calamities on this day—I trust Chen and Cai were not yet at an end.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred calamities on this one day—I trust even Chen and Cai had not yet ended.

sentences.zh: 乘虎口而獲濟，陵陽侯而迅往，得投憩於濮陽，實陶衞之舊壤。

translations.literal: Riding the tiger's mouth I obtained crossing; surmounting the lord of Yang I swiftly went forward, obtaining rest at Puyang—the old soil of Tao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Through the tiger's mouth I won crossing; over the lord of Yang I sped forward and found rest at Puyang—the old soil of Tao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 望鄉村而佇立，曾不遙之河廣。

translations.literal: Gazing at the village I stood and waited; the river's breadth was not far.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward the village I stood and waited; the river's breadth was not far.

sentences.zh: 聞虜馬之夕嘶，見胡塵之晝上。

translations.literal: I heard barbarian horses neigh at evening and saw Hu dust rise by day.
translations.idiomatic: I heard barbarian horses neigh at dusk and saw Hu dust rise by day.

sentences.zh: 王略恢而廟勝，車徒發而雷響。

translations.literal: The king's plan was broad and the temple victory sure; chariots and foot set out with thunder's roar.
translations.idiomatic: The royal plan was broad, the temple victory sure; chariots and foot set out with thunder's roar.

sentences.zh: 扇風師之猛氣，張天罼之層網。

translations.literal: They fanned the fierce breath of the wind-master and spread the layered net of Heaven's snare.
translations.idiomatic: They fanned the wind-master's fierce breath and spread Heaven's layered snare.

sentences.zh: 裁一鼓而冰銷，俄氛祲之廓蕩。

translations.literal: At one drum-stroke ice melted; soon the baleful vapors were cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: At one drum-stroke the ice melted; soon the baleful mists were cleared away.

sentences.zh: 昔蘧生之出奔，覩亡徵於亂政。

translations.literal: In former times when Master Qu fled, he saw the sign of ruin in disorder's governance.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when Master Qu fled, he saw ruin's sign in disorder's governance.

sentences.zh: 及季子之來反，乃君立而位定。

translations.literal: When the younger son returned in turn, then the lord was established and rank was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When the younger son returned in turn, the lord was established and rank was fixed.

sentences.zh: 伊吾人之蕞爾，本無傒於衰盛。

translations.literal: Ah, we people in our slightness—originally we did not look to decline or flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Ah—we people, slight as we are, never looked to decline or flourish.

sentences.zh: 忻草茅而偃伏，且優遊於辰慶。

translations.literal: Glad in thatched huts I lay prostrate and for a time wandered free in the year's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Glad in thatched huts I lay low and for a time wandered free in the year's blessing.

sentences.zh: 復推斥於宦流，延光華於璽命。

translations.literal: Again I was pushed aside in the stream of office and extended splendor in the seal's command.
translations.idiomatic: Again I was pushed aside in office's stream and extended splendor in the seal's command.

sentences.zh: 甫聞內侍之忝，復奉優加之令。

translations.literal: Just then I heard the shame of the inner attendant; again I received the order of added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Just then I heard the inner attendant's shame; again I received an order of added favor.

sentences.zh: 何金紫之陸離，鬱貂玉之相映。

translations.literal: What scattered gold and purple; sable and jade glowed against each other.
translations.idiomatic: What scattered gold and purple—sable and jade glowing against each other!

sentences.zh: 時權定之云初，尚民心之易擾。

translations.literal: At the time power was first settled and the people's hearts were still easy to disturb.
translations.idiomatic: At the time power was first settled and the people's hearts were still easily disturbed.

sentences.zh: 何建武之明傑，茂雄姿於天表。

translations.literal: What brilliance of Jianwu; what heroic bearing above heaven's brow.
translations.idiomatic: What brilliance in Jianwu; what heroic bearing above heaven's brow!

sentences.zh: 忽靈命之有歸，藉親均而爭紹。

translations.literal: Suddenly the spirit mandate had its return; leaning on kinship they contended for succession.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the spirit mandate turned homeward; leaning on kinship they contended for succession.

sentences.zh: 師出楚而飈發，旆陵江而雲矯。

translations.literal: Armies issued from Chu like a gale; banners crossed the river like clouds arching.
translations.idiomatic: Armies issued from Chu like a gale; banners crossed the river like arching clouds.

sentences.zh: 闢閶闔之崢嶸，端冕旒於億兆。

translations.literal: They opened the towering Changhe gate and set the crown and tassels before the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the towering Changhe gate and set crown and tassels before the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 神駕逝以流越，翠華飈而繚繞。

translations.literal: The spirit carriage passed in flowing flight; the emerald canopy streamed and circled.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit carriage passed in flowing flight; the emerald canopy streamed and wheeled.

sentences.zh: 苟命舛而數違，雖功深而祚天。

translations.literal: If fate is contrary and numbers oppose, though merit is deep the throne is heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: If fate turns contrary and numbers oppose, though merit runs deep the throne belongs to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時難忽然已及，網羅周其四張。

translations.literal: Hardship came suddenly and was already upon us; nets and snares surrounded on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hardship came suddenly and was already upon us; nets and snares closed on every side.

sentences.zh: 非五三之親暱，罕狥節於漢陽。

translations.literal: Not the kin of the Five Three; few followed integrity at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Not kin of the Five Three—few followed integrity at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 彼百僚之冠帶，咸北面於西王。

translations.literal: Those hundred officials in caps and sashes—all turned their faces north to the Western King.
translations.idiomatic: Those hundred officials in caps and sashes—all turned north to the Western King.

sentences.zh: 矧恩疏而任遠，固身存而義亡。

translations.literal: How much more when grace was distant and trust far—solid was the body kept, but righteousness was lost.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when grace was distant and trust far—the body was kept, but righteousness was lost.

sentences.zh: 及宸居之反正，振天網於頹綱。

translations.literal: When the imperial seat returned to right rule, the heaven-net was shaken out in the collapsed bonds.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne returned to right rule, the heaven-net was shaken out over collapsed bonds.

sentences.zh: 甄大義以明罰，虛半列於周行。

translations.literal: Discerning great righteousness to clarify punishment, half the ranks stood empty in the Zhou row.
translations.idiomatic: Discerning great righteousness to clarify punishment, half the ranks stood empty in the court row.

sentences.zh: 乃褫帶而來反，驅下澤於故鄉。

translations.literal: Then I was stripped of my belt and came back, driving the lower marsh to my old home.
translations.idiomatic: Then I was stripped of my belt and came back, driving my humble cart to my old home.

sentences.zh: 探宿志以內求，撫身途而自計。

translations.literal: I searched my old will within and stroked the path of my person to reckon for myself.
translations.idiomatic: I searched my old will within and traced my life's path to reckon for myself.

sentences.zh: 不詭遇以邀合，豈釣名以干世。

translations.literal: I did not meet fortune by crooked paths to seek alliance; how could I fish for fame to importune the age?
translations.idiomatic: I did not meet fortune by crooked paths to seek alliance; how could I fish for fame and importune the age?

sentences.zh: 獨浩然而任己，同虛舟之不繫。

translations.literal: Alone vast I entrusted myself to myself, like an empty boat that is not tied.
translations.idiomatic: Alone and vast I entrusted myself to myself, like an empty boat untied.

sentences.zh: 既未識其所以來，亦豈知其所以逝。

translations.literal: I had not yet known whence I came; how could I know whither I went?
translations.idiomatic: I had not yet known whence I came—how could I know whither I went?

sentences.zh: 於是得喪同遣，忘懷自深。

translations.literal: Thereupon gain and loss went the same road; forgetting lodged deep within.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon gain and loss took the same road; forgetting lodged deep within.

sentences.zh: 遇物栖息，觸地山林。

translations.literal: Meeting things I rested; touching earth I found mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting things, I rested; touching earth, I found mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 雖因西浮之迹，何異東都之心。

translations.literal: Though the trace floated westward, what differed from the heart of the eastern capital?
translations.idiomatic: Though my trace floated westward, what differed from the heart of the eastern capital?

sentences.zh: 願自託於魚鳥，永得性於飛沉。

translations.literal: I wished to entrust myself to fish and birds and forever keep my nature in flight and sinking.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to lodge with fish and birds and keep forever my nature in flight and depth.

sentences.zh: 庶保此以獲沒，不再罪於當今。

translations.literal: I hoped by keeping this to obtain burial and not again be guilty in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped by this to win a peaceful grave and not again be guilty in the present age.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，遭母憂，還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign he encountered mourning for his mother and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaojing's reign he went into mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 徵為魏尹，將軍如故，以禫制未終，表辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Intendant of Wei with his generalship as before; because the mourning period was not yet ended he submitted a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Intendant of Wei with his generalship unchanged, he declined because mourning was not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 朝議亦以為優，仍許其讓。

translations.literal: Court discussion too held this superior, and his refusal was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed his refusal was fitting and allowed it.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍求通和好，朝廷盛選行人，以諧兼散騎常侍，為聘使主。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sought communication and peace; the court carefully selected envoys and made Xie Concurrent Regular Attendant chief of the betrothal mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan sought peace, the court carefully chose envoys and made Xie Concurrent Regular Attendant head of the embassy.

sentences.zh: 諧至石頭，蕭衍遣其主客郎范胥當接。

translations.literal: When Xie reached Stone City, Xiao Yan sent his Chief of Receiving Guests, Gentleman Lang Fan Xu, to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie reached Stone City, Xiao Yan sent his Chief of Receiving Guests, Gentleman Lang Fan Xu, to receive him.

sentences.zh: 諧問胥曰：「主客在郎官幾時？」

translations.literal: Xie asked Xu: "How long has the Chief of Receiving Guests served as Gentleman Lang?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie asked Xu: "How long have you served as Gentleman Lang in the office of Chief of Receiving Guests?"

sentences.zh: 胥答曰：「我本訓冑虎門，適復今任。」

translations.literal: Xu answered: "I originally trained at the Tiger Gate, and have just now taken this post again."
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied: "I was trained at the Tiger Gate and have only just taken this post again."

sentences.zh: 諧言：「國子博士不應左轉為郎。」

translations.literal: Xie said: "A National University erudite ought not be transferred left to become a Gentleman Lang."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "A National University erudite ought not be demoted to Gentleman Lang."

sentences.zh: 胥答曰：「特為應接遠賓，故權兼耳。」

translations.literal: Xu answered: "It is specially to receive distant guests, so the concurrent appointment is temporary."
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied: "It is only to receive distant guests, so the concurrent post is temporary."

sentences.zh: 諧言：「屈己濟務，誠得事宜。

translations.literal: Xie said: "Bending oneself to serve affairs—truly this fits the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "Bending oneself to serve affairs—truly that fits the occasion.

sentences.zh: 由我一介行人，令卿左轉。」

translations.literal: Because of one lone envoy like me, it makes you transferred left."
translations.idiomatic: Because of one lone envoy like me, you have been demoted."

sentences.zh: 胥答曰：「自顧菲薄，不足對揚盛美，豈敢言屈。」

translations.literal: Xu answered: "Looking back on my slight worth, it is not enough to respond to and spread your great beauty—how dare I speak of being bent?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied: "Considering my slight worth, I am hardly fit to answer your gracious words—how dare I speak of being wronged?"

sentences.zh: 胥問曰：「今猶尚暖，北間當小寒於此？」

translations.literal: Xu asked: "It is still warm now—does the north have a little cold compared with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked: "It is still warm here—is the north a little colder than this?"

sentences.zh: 諧答曰：「地居陰陽之正，寒暑適時，不知多少。」

translations.literal: Xie answered: "The land occupies the correct balance of yin and yang; cold and heat come at the proper seasons—I do not know how much."
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "Our land sits in the balance of yin and yang; cold and heat come in their seasons—I could not say how much."

sentences.zh: 胥曰：「所訪鄴下，豈是測影之地？」

translations.literal: Xu said: "The place you ask about below Ye—is that a site for measuring shadows?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "The place you ask about below Ye—is that where one measures shadows?"

sentences.zh: 諧答曰：「皆是皇居帝里，相去不遠，可得統而言之。」

translations.literal: Xie answered: "They are all imperial residences and emperors' capitals; the distance is not great—they can be spoken of as one."
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "They are all imperial residences and emperors' capitals, not far apart—they may be spoken of as one."

sentences.zh: 胥曰：「洛陽既稱盛美，何事遷鄴？」

translations.literal: Xu said: "If Luoyang was called splendid and beautiful, why move the capital to Ye?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "If Luoyang was called splendid, why move the capital to Ye?"

sentences.zh: 諧答曰：「不常厥邑，于茲五邦，王者無外，所在關河，復何所怪？」

translations.literal: Xie answered: "Capitals are not fixed; to this point there have been five states. A king has no outside—all lies within the passes and rivers—what is there to wonder at?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "Capitals are not fixed; we have had five in succession. A king has no outside—all lies within the passes and rivers—what is strange in that?"

sentences.zh: 胥曰：「殷人否危，故遷相耿，貴朝何為而遷？」

translations.literal: Xu said: "The Yin people were in peril and danger, therefore they moved to Xiang and Geng—why does your exalted court move?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "The Yin moved when in peril—why does your exalted court move?"

sentences.zh: 諧答：「聖人藏往知來，相時而動，何必俟於隆替？」

translations.literal: Xie answered: "Sages store the past and know what is coming; they move according to the times—why must one wait for rise and fall?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "Sages store the past and know what comes; they move with the times—why wait for rise and fall?"

sentences.zh: 胥曰：「金陵王氣兆於先代，黃旗紫蓋，本出東南，君臨萬邦，故宜在此。」

translations.literal: Xu said: "Jinling's royal aura was portended in the former generation; the yellow flag and purple canopy originally came from the southeast—to lord the myriad states, therefore it should be here."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "Jinling's royal aura was foretold in the former age; the yellow flag and purple canopy came from the southeast—to rule the myriad states, it should be here."

sentences.zh: 諧答曰：「帝王符命，豈得與中國比隆？

translations.literal: Xie answered: "Imperial command and mandate—how can they be compared in splendor with the Central States?
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "Imperial mandate—how can it be compared in splendor with the Central States?

sentences.zh: 紫蓋黃旗，終於入洛，無乃自害也？

translations.literal: The purple canopy and yellow flag end by entering Luoyang—is this not harming yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: The purple canopy and yellow flag end by entering Luoyang—is that not self-harm?

sentences.zh: 有口之說，乃是俳諧，亦何足道！」

translations.literal: Talk with mouths is merely jest and banter—what is there worth speaking of!"
translations.idiomatic: Mouth-talk is merely jest and banter—what is there worth saying!"

sentences.zh: 蕭衍親問諧曰：「魏朝人士，德行四科之徒凡有幾人？」

translations.literal: Xiao Yan personally asked Xie: "Among the men of Wei in virtue and the four categories, how many are there in all?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan asked Xie in person: "Among Wei's men of virtue in the four categories, how many are there?"

sentences.zh: 諧對曰：「本朝多士，義等如林，文武賢才，布在列位，四科之美，非無其人，庸短造次，無以備啟。」

translations.literal: Xie replied: "Our court has many scholars, righteousness equal to a forest; civil and military worthies and talents are spread through the ranks—the beauty of the four categories is not without men, but my slightness in haste cannot fully report."
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "Our court has many scholars, righteous as a forest; civil and military talents fill the ranks—the four categories are not without men, but in my haste I cannot fully report."

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「武王有亂臣十人，魏雖人物之盛，豈得頓如卿言？」

translations.literal: Yan said: "King Wu had ten ministers in disorder—though Wei is rich in men, can it suddenly be as you say?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "King Wu had ten disorderly ministers—can Wei, rich as it is in men, suddenly match your claim?"

sentences.zh: 諧曰：「愚謂周稱十人，本舉佐命，至於『濟濟多士』，實是文王之詩。

translations.literal: Xie said: "I foolishly hold that Zhou's mention of ten men originally cited those who aided the mandate; as for 'the many scholars,' that is truly a poem of King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "I hold that Zhou's ten men originally cited those who aided the mandate; as for 'the many scholars,' that is truly King Wen's poem.

sentences.zh: 皇朝廊廟之才，足與周人有競。」

translations.literal: Our court's talent in the hall and temple is enough to rival the men of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Our court's hall-and-temple talent is enough to rival Zhou's men."

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「若爾，文足標異、武有冠絕者，便可指陳。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "If so, those whose literature suffices to mark them out and whose martial skill crowns all—point them out and state them."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "If so, name those whose literature marks them out and whose martial skill crowns all."

sentences.zh: 諧曰：「大丞相勃海王秉文經武，左右皇極，畫一九州，懸衡四海。

translations.literal: Xie said: "The Grand Chancellor, the Prince of Bohai, holds the literary and military classics and assists the imperial pole; he governs the nine provinces with one plan and hangs the balance over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "Grand Chancellor, the Prince of Bohai, holds the literary and military classics and assists the throne; he governs the nine provinces with one plan and holds the balance over the four seas.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書、汝陽王元叔昭、尚書令元世儁，宗室之秀，綰政朝端。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao, and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shijun—clan talents who hold the reins at court's head.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao, and Director Yuan Shijun—clan talents who hold the reins at court.

sentences.zh: 左僕射司馬子如、右僕射高隆之，並時譽民英，勠力匡輔。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi—both at the time famed as people's heroes, striving together in support.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi—both famed as heroes of the age, striving together in support.

sentences.zh: 侍中高岳、侍中孫騰，勳賢忠亮，宣讚王猷。

translations.literal: Attendant Gao Yue and Attendant Sun Teng—meritorious worthies, loyal and bright, proclaiming and spreading the king's design.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Gao Yue and Sun Teng—meritorious worthies, loyal and bright, proclaiming the king's design.

sentences.zh: 自餘才美不可具悉。」

translations.literal: The remaining talents and beauties cannot all be told in detail."
translations.idiomatic: The remaining talents cannot all be told in detail."

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「故宜輔弼幼主，永固基業，深不可言。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Therefore they should assist and support the young lord and forever solidify the foundation—profound beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "They should assist the young lord and forever solidify the foundation—profound beyond words."

sentences.zh: 江南稱其才辯。

translations.literal: The south of the river praised his talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river praised his wit and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 使還，除大司農卿，加驃騎將軍，轉祕書監。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he was made Grand Director of Agriculture, given the additional title Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made Grand Director of Agriculture, additionally Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遇偏風廢頓。

translations.literal: He encountered partial wind and was crippled.
translations.idiomatic: He was crippled by partial paralysis.

sentences.zh: 武定二年卒，年四十九，時人悼惜之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he died at age forty-nine; men of the time mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wuding 2 at forty-nine; contemporaries mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、衞尉卿、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of the Guard, and regional inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of the Guard, and regional inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 所著文集，別有集錄行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored were separately compiled and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated separately in the world.

sentences.zh: 長子嶽，武定末，司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yue, at the end of the Wuding era, was Libationer in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yue, at the end of Wuding, was Libationer in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 嶽弟庶，尚書南主客郎。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Shu was Gentleman of the Southern Receiving Guests in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's younger brother Shu served as Gentleman of the Southern Receiving Guests in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 諧弟邕，字修穆。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Yong, courtesy name Xiumu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother was Yong, styled Xiumu.

sentences.zh: 幼而儁爽，有逸才。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome and quick, with outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was handsome and quick, with exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎、高陽王雍友。

translations.literal: Assistant Compiler and friend to the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was Assistant Compiler and companion to the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong.

sentences.zh: 凡所交遊皆倍年，儁秀才藻之美，為時所稱。

translations.literal: All his companions were twice his age; the beauty of his talent and literary ornament was praised by the time.
translations.idiomatic: All his companions were twice his age; the beauty of his talent and literary ornament was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮遠將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Pacifies the Distance and regional inspector of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and regional inspector of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：邢巒以文武才策，當軍國之任，內參機揆，外寄折衝，其緯世之器歟？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xing Luan, with civil and military talent and stratagem, bore the burden of army and state; within he joined in secret counsel, outside he was entrusted with breaking the foe—was he not a vessel to weave the age?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xing Luan, with civil and military talent and stratagem, bore army and state; within he joined secret counsel, outside he broke the foe—was he not a vessel to weave the age?

sentences.zh: 李平以高明幹略，効智於時，出入當官，功名克著，蓋贊務之英也。

translations.literal: Li Ping, with lofty clarity and capable strategy, applied wisdom to the time; entering and leaving office, merit and fame were fully marked—he was indeed a hero of assisting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping, with lofty clarity and capable strategy, applied wisdom to his age; in every office merit and fame stood out—he was indeed a hero of statecraft.

translations.idiomatic: "Native of Mo in Hejian"—all editions wrongly read "Zheng" for "Mo"; corrected per Biography of Xing Luan, History of the North juan 43.

translations.idiomatic: reads "Lu."

sentences.zh: 按「魯方達」屢見卷八世宗紀正始二年、卷九八蕭衍傳，是這次戰事中梁朝重要將領。

translations.literal: Comment: "Lu Fangda" appears repeatedly in Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 2, juan 8, and Biography of Xiao Yan, juan 98—he was an important Liang commander in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Lu Fangda" appears repeatedly in Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 2, juan 8, and Biography of Xiao Yan, juan 98—an important Liang commander in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳中也幾次提到他，當時別無「曾方達」其人。

translations.literal: The Biography of Deng Yuanqi, juan 10 of the Book of Liang, also mentions him several times; at the time there was no other man called "Zeng Fangda."
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Deng Yuanqi, Book of Liang juan 10, also mentions him several times; there was no "Zeng Fangda" at the time.

sentences.zh: 「曾」乃「魯」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Zeng" is a corruption of "Lu"—now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Zeng" is a corruption of "Lu"—corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 蕭淵藻是裙屐少年 諸本「裙屐」作「羣劇」，北史卷四三、通鑑卷一四六

translations.literal: "Xiao Yuanzao was a silk-slipper youth"—in all editions "silk-slipper" is written "group drama"; History of the North juan 43, Zizhi tongjian juan 146
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao Yuanzao was a silk-slipper youth"—all editions read "group drama" for "silk-slipper"; History of the North juan 43, Zizhi tongjian juan 146

sentences.zh: 〈四五五二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4552〉

sentences.zh: 作「裙屐」。

translations.literal: reads "silk-slipper."
translations.idiomatic: reads "silk-slipper."

sentences.zh: 按「羣劇」無義，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: "group drama" is meaningless—now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "group drama" is meaningless—corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 便戮鄧元起 諸本「起」作「超」。

translations.literal: "Then executed Deng Yuanqi"—in all editions "Yuanqi" is written "Yuanchao."
translations.idiomatic: "Then executed Deng Yuanqi"—all editions read "Yuanchao" for "Yuanqi."

sentences.zh: 按蕭淵藻殺鄧元起，事見南史卷五五鄧元起傳。

translations.literal: Comment: Xiao Yuanzao's killing of Deng Yuanqi is recorded in Biography of Deng Yuanqi, juan 55 of the History of the South.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Xiao Yuanzao's killing of Deng Yuanqi is recorded in Biography of Deng Yuanqi, History of the South juan 55.

sentences.zh: 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳說元起「被收付州獄，於獄自縊」，微異，但死於淵藻之手的是鄧元起則一，「超」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Biography of Deng Yuanqi, juan 10 of the Book of Liang, says Yuanqi "was taken into the provincial prison and hanged himself in prison"—slightly different, but that Deng Yuanqi died at Yuanzao's hands is the same; "chao" is corrupt—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang juan 10 says Yuanqi "was taken into provincial prison and hanged himself"—slightly different, but that Yuanqi died at Yuanzao's hands is the same; "chao" is corrupt—corrected.

sentences.zh: 比建議之始 通鑑卷一四六

translations.literal: "When the proposal first began"—Zizhi tongjian juan 146
translations.idiomatic: "When the proposal first began"—Comprehensive Mirror juan 146

sentences.zh: 〈四五五四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4554〉

sentences.zh: 「比」下有「道遷」二字「議」作「義」。

translations.literal: After "bi" there are the two characters "Daoqian"; "yi" is written "yi" ( righteousness ).
translations.idiomatic: After "bi" appear the two characters "Daoqian"; "yi" ( deliberation ) is written "yi" ( righteousness ).

sentences.zh: 按上二字當是通鑑所增，「議」疑當作「義」。

translations.literal: Comment: The two characters above were probably added by the Tongjian; "yi" is suspected to should be "yi" ( righteousness ).
translations.idiomatic: Note: The two characters above were probably added by the Tongjian; "yi" is suspected to should read "yi" ( righteousness ).

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍相文玉等率眾一萬屯於孤山 冊府卷三一三

translations.literal: "General of Agile Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led a force of ten thousand and encamped at Gushan"—Cefu yuangui juan 313
translations.idiomatic: "General of Agile Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand men and encamped at Gushan"—Cefu yuangui juan 313

sentences.zh: 〈四一九六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4196〉
reads "Huan" for "Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: reads "Huan" for "Xiang."

sentences.zh: 按卷八世宗紀正始三年七月丙寅稱「衍將桓和寇孤山，陷固城」，八月壬寅又稱「邢巒破蕭衍將桓和於孤山」。

translations.literal: Comment: Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 3, seventh month, bingyin day, says "Yan's general Huan He invaded Gushan and took Gucheng"; eighth month, renyin day, again says "Xing Luan defeated Liang general Huan He at Gushan."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 3, seventh month bingyin, says "Yan's general Huan He invaded Gushan and took Gucheng"; eighth month renyin says "Xing Luan defeated Liang general Huan He at Gushan."

sentences.zh: 卷九八蕭衍傳同，並不見所謂「相文玉」。

translations.literal: Biography of Xiao Yan, juan 98, agrees, and the so-called "Xiang Wenyu" is nowhere seen.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xiao Yan juan 98 agrees, and "Xiang Wenyu" is nowhere seen.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一四六

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 146
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian juan 146

sentences.zh: 〈四五六三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4563〉

sentences.zh: 也作「桓和屯孤山」，而此傳下文兩見「文玉」，通鑑都作「和」。

translations.literal: also reads "Huan He encamped at Gushan," while in this biography "Wenyu" appears twice below, and in the Tongjian both read "He."
translations.idiomatic: also reads "Huan He encamped at Gushan," while in this biography "Wenyu" appears twice below, and the Tongjian reads "He" both times.

sentences.zh: 則司馬光所見魏書當作「桓文玉」，故認為「文玉」即「桓和」。

translations.literal: Thus the Wei shu Sima Guang saw should read "Huan Wenyu," and he believed "Wenyu" was "Huan He."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Wei shu Sima Guang saw should read "Huan Wenyu," and he took "Wenyu" to be "Huan He."

sentences.zh: 這裏「相」當是「桓」之訛，「文玉」或是和字。

translations.literal: Here "Xiang" should be a corruption of "Huan"; "Wenyu" may be the character "he" in Huan He's name.
translations.idiomatic: Here "Xiang" is likely a corruption of "Huan"; "Wenyu" may represent the character "he" in Huan He's name.

sentences.zh: 而懷恭等復於清南造城 諸本「清」作「淮」，冊府卷三五三

translations.literal: "While Huai Gong and others again built a city at Qingnan"—in all editions "Qing" is written "Huai"; Cefu yuangui juan 353
translations.idiomatic: "While Huai Gong and others again built a city at Qingnan"—all editions read "Huai" for "Qing"; Cefu yuangui juan 353

sentences.zh: 〈四一九六頁〉、
通鑑卷一四六

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 146
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian juan 146

sentences.zh: 〈四五六四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4564〉
reads "Qing" for "Huai."
translations.idiomatic: reads "Qing" for "Huai."

sentences.zh: 按宿豫城在泗水即清水旁，「淮」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: Suyu city stood beside the Si River, which is the Qing River—"Huai" is corrupt; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Suyu city stood beside the Si River, which is the Qing River—"Huai" is corrupt; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 非可抑為必勝 諸本「勝」字闕，今據冊府卷四０四

translations.literal: "It cannot be suppressed into certain victory"—in all editions the character "sheng" ( victory ) is missing; now supplemented according to Cefu yuangui juan 404
translations.idiomatic: "It cannot be suppressed into certain victory"—all editions omit "sheng" ( victory ); supplemented per Cefu yuangui juan 404

sentences.zh: 〈四八０七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4807〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: supplemented.

sentences.zh: 蕭密餘軍猶自在彼 按「蕭密」即梁臨川王蕭宏，卷八世宗紀正始三年四月作「蕭容」，「密」「容」都是避元宏諱改。

translations.literal: "Xiao Mi's remaining army is still there"—Comment: "Xiao Mi" is Liang Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong; Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 3, fourth month, juan 8, reads "Xiao Rong"—both "Mi" and "Rong" are changes to avoid the taboo on Yuan Hong.
translations.idiomatic: "Xiao Mi's remaining army is still there"—Note: "Xiao Mi" is Liang Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong; Annals of Emperor Shizong, Zhengshi 3, fourth month, juan 8, reads "Xiao Rong"—both "Mi" and "Rong" avoid the taboo on Yuan Hong.

sentences.zh: 參卷八校記[一二]。

translations.literal: See Collation Note [12] to juan 8.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note [12] in juan 8.

sentences.zh: 喪元隸豎 諸本「豎」訛「賢」，不可解，今據冊府卷四二八

translations.literal: "Lost his head to the slave Shu"—in all editions "Shu" is wrongly written "Xian," which cannot be understood; now corrected according to Cefu yuangui juan 428
translations.idiomatic: "Lost his head to the slave Shu"—all editions wrongly read "Xian" for "Shu," which cannot be understood; corrected per Cefu yuangui juan 428

sentences.zh: 〈五０九九頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 5099〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: corrected.
translations.idiomatic: corrected.

sentences.zh: 度公之在彼 諸本此句作「兼云□公在彼」，不可解，今據冊府

translations.literal: "When Duke Du was there"—in all editions this line reads "Also saying [lacuna] Duke was there," which cannot be understood; now supplemented and corrected according to Cefu
translations.idiomatic: "When Duke Du was there"—all editions read "Also saying [lacuna] Duke was there," which cannot be understood; supplemented and corrected per Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same juan and page as above〉

sentences.zh: 補改。

translations.literal: supplemented and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: supplemented and corrected.

sentences.zh: 所製詩賦箴諫詠頌 按「諫」非文體之名，疑是「誄」之訛。

translations.literal: "The poems, fu, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and encomia he composed"—Comment: "remonstrance" ( jian ) is not a genre name; it is suspected to be a corruption of "elegy" ( lei ).
translations.idiomatic: "The poems, fu, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and encomia he composed"—Note: "remonstrance" ( jian ) is not a genre name; suspected corruption of "elegy" ( lei ).
